articles.title: This magazine plays Tetris — here’s how
articles.summary: Red Bull enlisted the creator of the Arduboy to create a thin and flexible version of Tetris embedded in the cover of its GamePop magazine.
articles.body: Tetris has been immortalized in a playable McDonald’s plastic chicken nugget, a playable fake 7-Eleven Slurpee cup, and a playable wristwatch. But the most intriguing way to play Tetris yet is encased in paper. Last year the Tetris Company partnered with Red Bull for a gaming tournament that culminated in the 150-meter-tall Dubai Frame landmark being turned into the world’s largest playable Tetris installation using over 2,000 drones that functioned as pixels. Although the timing was a coincidence, Red Bull also published a 180-page gaming edition of its The Red Bulletin lifestyle magazine around the same time as the event, with a limited number of copies wrapped in a less grandiose, but no less technically impressive, version of Alexey Pajitnov’s iconic puzzle game. [Media: To create a playable gaming magazine, Red Bull Media House (the company’s media wing) enlisted the help of Kevin Bates, who in 2014 wowed the internet by creating an ultra-thin Tetris-playing business card. In 2015, he launched the $39 Arduboy, a credit card-sized, open-source handheld that attracted a thriving community of developers. Over the course of a decade, Bates also created a pair of equally pocketable Tetris-playing handhelds that cost less than $30, and the shrunken-down USB-C Arduboy Mini. The GamePop GP-1 Playable Magazine System (as it’s officially called) is the latest evolution of Bates’ mission to use existing, accessible, and affordable technologies to reimagine what a portable gaming device can be. It took “most of last year” to develop, Bates revealed during a call with The Verge. He wouldn’t divulge the exact details of how his collaboration with Red Bull came to be. But if you’re looking to make an officially licensed version of Tetris that’s thin enough to flex, Bates has the experience, and he shared with us some of the technical details that make this creation work. [Image: The game’s screen is made up of 180 tiny RGB LEDs on a custom circuit board that can flex and bend. While OLED display technology has given us tablet-sized devices that fold into smartphones, they’re still expensive and fragile. To make a display that can survive being embedded in a flexible magazine cover without reinforcement, Bates created a custom matrix of 180 2mm RGB LEDs mounted to a flexible circuit board just 0.1mm thick. While the display and coin-cell batteries make it thicker in a few places — nearly 5mm at its thickest point — you genuinely feel like you’re playing a handheld made of paper. The flexible circuits are bonded between two sheets of paper to create the sleeve that wraps around the book-sized magazine, and it feels satisfyingly thin and flexible. Flexible circuits aren’t a new idea. They’ve been used in electronics for decades. You can find them in flip phones old enough they now feel like antiques, and nearly every laptop. They’re also frequently used to miniaturize devices that don’t fold or flex at all, connecting internal components where space is extremely limited. But it’s only in the past five or six years that the technology has become available to smaller makers, and Bates says he’s been “messing around with the flexible circuits for about as much time.” This collaboration was an opportunity to use what he’s learned to create a device that would live outside his workshop. The GamePop GP-1’s display resolution pales in comparison to the OLED screens used in folding phones, but Bates’ creation is far more durable. The game has not only undergone the typical safety tests, but Bates even “hit it with a hammer a few times” to test its durability. His display survived, but don’t try that with a folding phone. They’re still far less durable. [Image: To keep it as thin as possible, the Tetris game uses embedded touch sensors instead of physical buttons. Instead of buttons, the game uses seven capacitive touch sensors that are directly “printed in the copper layer of the board,” Bates says. There’s no true mechanical feedback when pressed, but the paper’s flex helps them feel a bit like a button when you press down. Bates says the responsiveness of the sensors was specifically tuned to account for the thickness of the paper stock and the glues used in the final print run. You’re not going to be chasing Tetris world records on the cover of a magazine, but the controls are satisfyingly responsive and the game is surprisingly much easier to play than other Tetris devices I’ve tested. [Image: Most of the game is made using flexible electronics, but there is a thin rigid PCB housing its processor and rechargeable batteries. How much does a flexible Tetris game cost to manufacture? Neither Bates nor Red Bull would divulge the total price tag for all the off-the-shelf and custom components you’ll find sandwiched inside the magazine’s cover. But to help keep costs down, not all components are flexible. Inside the edge of the cover, next to the magazine’s spine, you’ll find a long but thin rigid PCB where an ARM-based 32-bit microprocessor is located, along with four rechargeable LIR2016 3V coin cell batteries. [Image: The magazine features a deconstructed USB-C charging port along the bottom edge of its cover. Like most devices now, the game can be recharged using a USB-C cable, but it’s not immediately obvious where. Hidden along the bottom edge of the magazine’s cover is a deconstructed USB-C port. Instead of a metal ring, its socket is a small paper pocket containing a pin-covered head inside. It doesn’t feel quite as durable as the charging port on your phone, but it’s a welcome alternative to making the game disposable when the batteries die. Bates did have to cut some corners. The GamePop GP-1 saves high scores, but modern Tetris gameplay features, like previews of upcoming pieces and being able to save tetrominoes for later, aren’t included. There’s sound effects, but when starting a game you only hear a small snippet of the iconic Tetris theme. The game’s piezo speaker “uses about as much energy as it does to run the rest of the system,” Bates says, so this helps prolong the life of the small rechargeable batteries. He tells us you can play for an hour or two that way, and the battery should last many months when not in use. Red Bull made around 1,000 copies of the magazine. It’s only available online in Europe, but can also be found in some stores and newsstands, including Iconic Magazines in New York and Rare Mags outside Manchester in the UK. However, only 150 copies with the playable cover were produced, and none were made available to the public. They were distributed to Tetris competitors, those featured in the magazine, influencers, and select media. The playable cover isn’t going to revolutionize the print industry, or pave the way for smartphones we can roll up and stick in our back pockets. The goal was to use existing tech in a way that gamers haven’t seen before. Photography by Andrew Liszewski / The Verge

The Belmonts are finally back, baby. Plus, they're really in for an ass-kicking in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, a title seemingly designed to punish the vampire hunters more than ever before. Thankfully, there are ways to help Rose along her journey, such as the Brave Heart Fragments, which expand her health bar when you collect four pieces. So if you're one of the many people taking to the streets of Paris to try and extinguish Dracula's flame for the final time, here is the IGN guide covering exactly where to find every Brave Heart Fragment in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse.

articles.body:
In the Leonida Keys, Jason is out fishing for an unusual treasure with his friend Cal: bricks of cocaine. After a short cutscene introducing Chapter 1 – Just Like Paradise and the two talking, you'll begin the first mission in Grand Theft Auto VI , Gone Fishing, which features Jason getting Donnie out of a mess of Donnie’s own making. This official GTA 6 guide walks you through the Gone Fishing main mission.

Click on a link below to jump to that specific section of this guide:

The first vehicle you drive in GTA 6 is the boat: a unique Lure Predator. Pull up to the dropped cocaine package by holding R2 / RT to move forward, and ease on the speed as you approach.

Slow down the boat by pressing L2 / LT and keep holding it to reverse if you overshoot the target. You can focus on the objective location by pressing Left Stick Click + Right Stick Click / Left Stick Click + Right Stick Click simultaneously. This activates Focus Mode, causing the world around you to turn grey, and the beeping on the package emits a visible ripple, indicating its location. Press the thumbsticks again to return perception to normal.

Once you're close enough to the package marked by a pink arrow, Cal moves up and scoops the wrapped brick of cocaine out of the water. If you're not close enough or overshoot the package, Cal complains and you'll need to adjust the position of the boat.

With the first package collected, you’re instructed to follow Donnie’s plane, which should be conveniently going straight ahead. While you can try to see where it is in the sky, its location is also tracked on the minimap in the lower left .

Press D-pad Down on the D-Pad to see Donnie’s plane marked in the sky by a pink arrow along with other helpful mission, vehicle, and character status information.

Pressing D-pad Down on the D-Pad reveals the following information:

Stats Meters : In the top left, you’ll find the meters for: Health – The pink meter. If you take damage, your health slowly recovers over time. Stamina – The turquoise meter that determines how long you can sprint, jump, and perform other physically demanding activities. Focus – The purple meter tied to a variation of Focus unlocked at a later point.

Health – The pink meter. If you take damage, your health slowly recovers over time.

Stamina – The turquoise meter that determines how long you can sprint, jump, and perform other physically demanding activities.

Focus – The purple meter tied to a variation of Focus unlocked at a later point.

Vehicle Details : On the bottom left above the minimap, you’ll see details about the vehicle you’re in. The left engine icon shows the engine’s health status and the right fuel pump icon indicates the amount of fuel left in the vehicle.

Cash : On the top right you’ll see how much cash you have on hand.

You can also add additional navigation information to this extended HUD, like a compass, in the Settings. You’ll find the compass and others under Settings > UI. Then, scroll down to the Navigation section. Here you’ll see options for the minimap, compass, and more.

Meanwhile, Donnie, the man dropping the skimmed cocaine from a delivery he's supposed to be making, will fly overhead as you’re instructed to follow him to the next package, which should be a mostly straight shot from your location. Like before, slow down as you approach and let Cal hook the package. If you don’t quite see where it is, you can always press D-pad Down on the D-Pad to see it marked.

You’ve got one more drop to pick up, and this time you’ll need to do more meaningful navigation. Follow the plane by driving west and keep an eye on the pink waypoint on the minimap. It’ll only be a few seconds before Donnie calls out that he’s made the last drop.

The last package is dropped northwest of the second location. As noted, you can make sharper turns while driving by pressing Cross / A , and this is particularly helpful at higher speeds. Make your way to the third package, navigating around the islands and other obstacles in the water as needed. Like before, slowly approach the package when Cal calls it out and let him bring it onto the boat.

While on your way to the third package Donnie drops, you’ll get a tooltip for different camera options. Hold D-pad Down on the D-Pad to see the following options:

Cinematic : This mode pulls out the camera sometimes drastically, and sometimes focuses on a character or part of the vehicle. Hold D-pad Down to exit cinematic mode.

Markers : Press L1 / LB or R1 / RB to toggle between objective points. When only one is present, you’ll only jump to the one point.

Camera 1/2/3 : Pressing Square / X changes the zoom level of the standard camera, with 1 being the closest, 2 as the default, and 3 the most zoomed out level.

Once you’ve got all three packages, Donnie requests Jason and Cal watch his back while he makes the delivery to the Kingfishers, just in case things go sideways. The way to the plane takes you from Gambit Bay all the way into Cottonmouth Lake, where you’ll need to navigate between more narrow waterways, between scattered islands and bridges. The path is marked by a dotted pink line on the minimap that provides helpful directions on exactly where to go. You can also view the complete path by opening the Map.

Drive the boat a little less than a half mile through the islands to reach Donnie.

When you get close to the objective, Cal calls out the plane and the game takes over pulling the boat up into position. Jason moves toward the front to watch the deal go down. To get a better view of what’s happening, you’ll need to use binoculars. Do so by:

In the Weapons tab (the loadout opens to this by default), use Right Stick to navigate down to the highlighted binoculars.

Release L1 / LB while the binoculars are highlighted on the loadout wheel.

With the binoculars equipped, press L2 / LT (you don’t need to hold it down) to bring up the binoculars. Zoom in or out with D-pad Up and D-pad Down on the D-Pad, and watch Donnie as he approaches the Kingfishers.

The Kingfishers are rightfully suspicious of Donnie’s nosebleed and require him to join them deeper in the camp to check on the details of what was supposed to be delivered. Jason tells Cal to pull up on the side of the camp, assuming Donnie is in trouble. Cal does so and reluctantly hands Jason a gun. It’s time to find out what the Kingfishers want to do with Donnie.

Jason exits the boat and walks up the decaying dock. As you get closer to the RV Park you’ll get a tooltip that says you can crouch by pressing Circle / B to move quietly. Move forward and either hide in the trailer on the left and listen into the Kingfishers’ conversation to get more information about the situation or go past it to cut to the chase of rescuing Donnie.

This tutorial mission serves as an overview for stealth and combat in enemy territory. You can approach this section in many ways: with stealth, by going in loud and shoot enemies as you find them, or a combination of the two. Many of GTA 6’s missions allow you to take them on in your own playstyle with multiple paths and solutions to problems. This walkthrough details two of the many possible paths: how to rescue Donnie with stealth, or if you’d prefer the bold sort of rescue, how to shoot through the Kingfishers’ camp.

For this mission, I recommend starting with stealth and maintaining it for as long as possible. Doing so allows you to learn how enemies identify you when you’re trespassing, if they spot you at all. The severity of violence you exercise impacts more than the set of enemies ahead of you, though, so play with how you want to be perceived by others in mind. More on that later! For now, what’s most important is saving Donnie.

Open one (or both!) of the sections below to continue the walkthrough:

If you choose to fight your way to Donnie, expect plenty of return fire throughout the camp and periodic enemy reinforcements. As soon as you’re off the boat, you get on a call with a frantic Donnie trying – and failing – to play it cool. As soon as you start shooting, you’ll hear Donnie rush to describe where he’s being taken. He says you’re looking for a shack by a turbine. This is marked in pink on your map. Not long after, Cal calls in and Jason tells him to leave and that they’ll regroup back at Brian’s. Here are some things to keep in mind as you make your way to Donnie from the boat:

The additional Kingfishers arrive in trucks and boats. Some are bold and run at you, while others will hang back and shoot from cover. It’s easy to get surrounded here if you stay in one spot too long, so keep moving.

You’ll need to take cover too if you want to survive the onslaught of Kingfisher bullets. Move to cover quickly by tapping R1 / RB .

You won’t get the primary source of healing in GTAVI - Zombix - until you find Donnie, which can make this section more difficult if you get surrounded before you reach him.

As you shoot enemies, you may notice a yellow or red hit marker paired with a flash of the same color around the screen. This indicates how you’ve put an end to an enemy. Yellow means you’ve achieved a non-lethal incapacitation. Red means you’ve lethally put an end to them. You’ll likely get the non-lethal takedown with blunt melee weapons and shots to the legs, arms, and belly. Successful head shots to unarmored enemies will always be an instant lethal kill.

The way you eliminate targets reflects on your Criminal Profile , as noted periodically by various devil face pop-ups on the right side of the screen. You’ll learn more about the Criminal Profile in an upcoming mission. If you’re eager to know more now, you can read about the Criminal Profile in the Help menu or visit our Criminal Profile guide.

The Kingfishers' camp has explosives scattered around that can help you in a pinch, though. You can find them more easily by entering Focus (press Left Stick Click + Right Stick Click simultaneously). Enemies are also highlighted in red when Focus is active. Focus cancels when you aim down sights or when you press the thumbsticks again.

Jason’s starting pistol is nice, but a rifle or shotgun might do you better. As you slay Kingfishers in the camp, you can pick up weapons they drop by pressing L1 / LB . If you find a quiet moment, loot the fallen corpses by pressing Triangle / Y while standing over them to get more ammo. In the future, you’ll find more than ammo on your fallen enemies .

In addition to using Focus to find where enemies are hiding, pay attention to the yellow light that fades and brightens along the edge of the screen . This indicates an enemy’s location. The brighter it is, the closer they are.

You’ll find Donnie in the large shack by the turbine. A brief cutscene kicks off as you get close.

Before you can free Donnie, you’ll need to punch out the big Kingfisher that enters behind you. You can’t pull your gun on him, but he’ll go down after quite a few punches. Do your best to get his back to the table or a shelf to end the fight faster.

After you’ve got Donnie, he’ll get you a bottle of Zombix - medicine that’ll restore your health. The Kingfishers start shooting into the shack, giving you little time to make your next move. Make sure your weapon is reloaded then break through the double doors to the next objective: Head for the Plane.

Outside, the Kingfishers swarm. Some come from the entrance side of the shack, but plenty more will be ahead of you. Like before, it’s crucial you take cover to avoid taking too much damage. Keep an eye on Donnie, too . If he dies, you’ll fail the mission and have to restart at the last checkpoint.

As you cut down the Kingfishers, Donnie mentions that the money they’re owed is in a trailer on the way to the plane. You don’t have to get it, but why say no to money? The Kingfishers fiercely protect the trailer and their people will keep coming from all sides of the camp, so be quick about going to get the money if you choose to. Most of the trucks that pull up are unlocked. Food for thought!

Optional: Recover the Cash from the Trailer

Walk inside the trailer and a man jumps Jason with a knife. Press Square / X quickly, and Jason will knock out the foe instantly. Grab the Zombix from the counter (especially if you’ve chosen violence), then move forward and grab Brian’s cash from the back of the trailer. Get to the docks with Donnie when you’re ready to leave. Instead of pressing Triangle / Y to enter the plane, all you need to do is walk up to kick off the next part. Click or tap here to skip to Fly Back to Brian’s Marina .

Below is a mapped stealth path that’ll lead you to Donnie’s location, though this is only one of many ways to Donnie’s location. If you haven’t already left the wagon, do so and go straight forward toward the man with his back to you. When you get close to the man, hold R2 / RT to grab the man by surprise then rapidly press Square / X to knock him out. You'll see a yellow flash which notes you've successfully completed a non-lethal takedown.

Before moving forward, don't forget to loot the body for ammo. You might find money and illicit goods on incapacitated folks throughout your time in Leonida, too. You can also pick up and wear hats or sunglasses dropped by opponents, as well as carry their guns by pressing L1 / LB when you spot them on the ground. In this case, you’ll get a Wortham W-14 combat rifle. You won’t keep any guns you loot from this mission, but picking them up now still adds them to your tracked collection.

Don't be alarmed; there are bears, tigers, and other dangerous animals everywhere! Stay crouched and move straight ahead between the row of cages.

As you move forward, Donnie reveals hints about his location. When the Right Stick Click / Right Stick Click prompt flashes on the bottom right to show the turbine's location, hold Right Stick Click / Right Stick Click to fill the meter on the bottom right to shift your camera to the turbine. That’s about where Donnie is.

If you press Left Stick Click + Right Stick Click / Left Stick Click + Right Stick Click , you’ll also see the wind from the turbine, along with enemies highlighted in red . When the two thumbsticks are pressed together, you enter Focus Mode, a state where time slows down and important items, enemies and allies, weapons, and objectives are highlighted. Use it as you need extra help navigating.

Move forward a bit and after you pass the barking dog, start moving right toward the tall grass and the pond. You’ll enter the tall grass after you pass the smaller empty bird cages.

Continue through the grass along the pond, being careful to keep crouching. Keep an eye on the few Kingfishers on the right, too. They’ll move, but they shouldn’t spot you on the bank of the pond so long as you keep to the grass.

Move out of the grass once you reach the pond’s dock and continue forward. You can go left and knock out the guy in the red shirt, but it’s safer to stay in the shadows on the right side of the cages. The shack Donnie is being held in is close! It’s just across the dirt road. Make sure the coast is clear and walk quietly across, aiming for the side of the dingy trailer with the green stripe for cover. Then, wrap around the trailer by going left into the bushes. Don’t worry, the two guys just beyond continue straight ahead rather than turning around, as long as you stay crouched and quiet.

From the bushes, cross the next dirt road toward the RV Park sign quietly.

As you come around the wooden Sunrise RV Park sign, wait for the man working on his truck to walk away . When he’s gone, you have a clear shot to the shack where they’re keeping Donnie.

You can double check to see if enemies are around by pressing Left Stick Click + Right Stick Click / Left Stick Click + Right Stick Click to enter Focus Mode.

Scoot into the building where Donnie is being held captive – the white door in front is open, so you only need to push in to enter.

If you're spotted here, don't sweat it! Move quickly inside to help Donnie and untie him by pressing Triangle / Y . As soon as you have Donnie free, a man walks in, angry. Rapidly press Square / X to escape his hold, then keep pressing Square / X to fight. A few punches later and he’ll be out cold.

Donnie is free and passes over a bottle of Zombix he discovered in the room. Pick it up from the top of the fish tank with Triangle / Y .

Now that you’ve got it, you can heal by holding L1 / LB and then pressing Square / X .

There’s not much in the shack aside from pistol ammo and a knife on the workbench, so leave whenever you’re ready – Donnie is eager to go. Be sure to exit crouched if you’re still playing stealth .

Donnie will follow your lead and won’t risk you being discovered, though he does get a little ahead to start with. Press R1 / RB to join Donnie in hiding, but you’re not going straight ahead. You can, and this is a good opportunity to get into a gun fight if you’re eager to. If you do just make sure Donnie doesn't get left too far behind with Kingfishers. He'll fight alongside you, but his shooting skills will only carry him so far. If Donnie dies, you'll fail and need to restart from the last checkpoint. As the Kingfishers move about, Donnie mentions cash in the trailer not far off, but there are a bunch of Kingfishers between it and you. To keep moving through this area with stealth, step back a bit and go right from your location to move between the empty bird cages.

While you’re doing this, someone will call out that Donnie is missing. There’s no way we’re passing up on a payout, so let’s go complete that optional objective next.

Keep right and toward the tree line, moving behind a small building. As you progress another truck full of Kingfishers pulls up, increasing their numbers even more. So long as you stay quiet, low, and in the shadows, you should be okay, no matter what Donnie says. Move forward and into a building that’s got a clear “No Trespassing” sign. This building is empty of Kingfishers but filled with goodies. Enter Focus Mode and you’ll spot a highlighted Moreland 850 Shotgun, ammo, and plenty of explosive items around. Grab whatever you want from here and then move toward the open wall. Remember, you won’t keep the weapons you pick up in this mission.

Be careful moving out of the building. A blue truck drives up with two more men and parks not far from your position. Wait until the two walk off . Listen for when Jason calls for Donnie to wait, and a man exits the trailer. Wait for him to walk off before moving across the dirt road toward the trailer. Get ready for a…jump scare? Walk inside the trailer and a man jumps Jason with a knife. Press Square / X quickly, and Jason will knock out the foe instantly. Grab the Zombix from the counter (you can never have too much Zombix!), then move forward and grab Brian’s cash from the back of the trailer.

With the cash in hand, move out of the trailer quickly, and move across the road to Donnie fast, using the right side of the white shipping container for cover.

Not far off, an airboat is pulling up with others that can spot you if you take too long crossing the road and getting into cover. Sneak through the bushes near the dock, then once the new arrivals walk off, stay crouched but press Left Stick Click / Left Stick Click to move quickly across the dock.

Run to the sea plane and Jason will automatically get in once you’re close enough, followed by Donnie. As Jason scoots in and starts up the plane, the Kingfishers notice and start shooting. Time to get out of here.

To fly the plane, use R2 / RT to accelerate and as you gain speed, pull down on the left thumbstick ( Left Stick ) to take off. You’ll sustain some engine damage in the takeoff, but there isn’t much that you can do to prevent that other than to get as high as you can as quickly as possible.

With the danger behind them, Donnie checks in on Jason. Did you get the cash from the trailer? So long as you did, you’ll at least get some sort of payout from the boss, Brian - but only after he gets his. Look at the minimap (or map by pressing Touchpad or from the pause menu) to see your next destination: Brian’s Marina.

It should only be about a mile away. As you turn toward its direction, you’ll get a short cutscene featuring Donnie’s nerves and a scene that depends on your actions in the Kingfishers camp. Once you’re back in control of the plane, it’s already time to land! You’re in a seaplane so you won’t need to worry about putting down landing gear for the water.

Press L2 / LT to slow down as you get closer to the water (if you don’t slow down enough, Donnie will berate you). Gently touch down in the water and tap R2 / RT to give the engine a bit of power as you taxi to Brian’s Marina. As noted by the tool tip, you can use Square / X and Circle / B to turn more sharply, which is especially helpful when taxiing.

As you approach the marina in the plane, Donnie does one final freakout about the situation in a cutscene while Jason parks. The cutscene continues with Brian’s introduction and his sly interrogation of Donnie as soon as he realizes things have gone wrong.

Whether or not you collected the money changes the scene a bit, but regardless, Brian isn’t happy with Donnie. Brian then asks Jason for the real story before giving Jason a brief scolding and sends him off.

Cal and Jason leave together, worried. Continue walking through the parking lot toward Jason’s truck, the old, rough-looking car in the light. Enter the car by pressing Triangle / Y . The GPS in the bottom left will guide you to Cal’s house, though you can look at the map to see the full path. If you turn early or choose to go a different way, the GPS adjusts directions automatically.

Back out of the parking spot by pressing L2 / LT , then use R2 / RT to approach the gate and wait for it to open. As potentially your first time driving on the streets of Leonida, I’d recommend participating in some basic driving safety to avoid damaging or destroying your only car – damage will cost you later. Look left before you go forward ( other cars may hit you if you drive out in front of them ), but you can cut straight across the intersection to get on the road leading toward Cal’s house. As you drive, Jason and Cal discuss the potential ramifications of the Kingfishers deal gone wrong.

If you’d like, you can use the car’s blinkers by pressing D-pad Right or D-pad Left on the D-Pad. Once you make the turn, the blinker automatically turns off.

Cal’s place has a blue light on and sits at the end of the row. Pull into the driveway, and Cal leaves in a short cutscene where he expresses his worry about the danger they’ve suddenly found themselves in – and his worry that Jason specifically might get hurt. They part, and Jason finally gets to go home.

Back out of the driveway and take the road back to the main street, using the GPS to get home. You don’t have to follow the standard rules of the road when driving in GTAVI, but you can get in trouble with the cops if you cause major accidents or hit pedestrians. Worse, if your car sustains damage, you’ll usually need to pay to get it fixed. While most damage received from mild crashes is cosmetic, you can damage or destroy the engine if you collide with something fast enough (especially if you ram into a tall tree or a utility pole). If that happens, you may not be able to drive the car at all until you get it towed. Driving quickly around other cars, cutting them off, or going offroad to take shortcuts is no problem, though, so drive however is most fun for you.

The streets aren’t too busy tonight. As you drive, you’ll get a tooltip explaining how to access the radio and other car settings. Press and hold D-pad Left on the D-Pad to scroll through the various radio stations, or use Right Stick to view a vehicle’s controls, including changing how headlights function, turning on hazards, and more.

Jason’s house is also secluded, just past a pink lit house and another lit with blue lights. Pull into the driveway and Jason will exit the car automatically (normally you’ll press Triangle / Y ). Take the stairs up and, as you do, Jason gets a call from Lucia. Enter the house to begin a cutscene conversation between Jason and Lucia as they talk about Lucia’s potential early release and their plan for her to move in if (when) it happens. Jason’s got a lot of work to do if he wants to get the house in decent shape.

The scene shifts to Jason working on fixing the leaky roof when Brian shows up with a list of tasks for him. A few folks owe Brian money, and Cal skipped out on work. It’s all Jason’s problem now.

A short introduction to the house plays, and then you’re free to go where you wish! You can change Jason’s clothes at the wardrobe, feed his pet snake Dolores, or explore beyond the house. Your rewards for the work you just did will be delivered as soon as you leave.

Donnie texts (view it when the notification pops up by pressing D-pad Up on the D-Pad), saying he left your pay for the skimmed bricks in the mailbox. You can text him back or ignore him. What you say to him can alter how he replies, but it doesn’t have a major impact on anything.

Grab your money from the mailbox, and you’re done with Gone Fishing. You'll receive between $100 and $220 as your reward , depending on how successful the mission was.

Congratulations on completing your first main mission in GTAVI! If you haven’t saved your game, go ahead and do that in the main menu. Select Game, then you’ll see Save Game, Load Game, and New Game. There’s an auto-save, but you also have 15 save slots to work with should you wish to return to an earlier save.

I recommend looking at the Settings to tweak the game to your liking too (something you should keep doing throughout Chapter 1). You can change things like the GPS voice, the size of the minimap, toggle the compass, turn off gore, and tons more. Visit the Settings Guide for suggestions on what to change and learn about other new useful features in GTA 6.

Other than that, I recommend sticking with the story for a while longer. There’s a ton to do, but you’ll get more out of it after you’ve unlocked some basic gameplay mechanics by playing through the story. You have three options for the next missions. Below is our recommended order:

articles.title: Coming Home Walkthrough - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: In the Coming Home main mission in Grand Theft Auto VI, Lucia was approved for early home release, and it’s time to pick her up. This official IGN GTA 6
articles.body:
In the Coming Home main mission in Grand Theft Auto VI , Lucia was approved for early home release, and it’s time to pick her up. This official IGN GTA 6 guide walks you through how to complete the Chapter 1 mission, Coming Home.

Click on a link below to jump to that specific section of this guide:

This mission is available after Lucia calls Jason from the penitentiary. If you don’t want to wait until the next day for her to call, you can go to bed and sleep to pass the time. As soon as Jason wakes up in the morning, Lucia calls and asks Jason to pick her up. When you’re ready, hop in the truck (with her change of clothes in the trunk, if you picked them up from Andy) and head to north Hamlet to get Lucia. Approaching the prison kicks off the mission.

When you’re .12 mi from the prison, a short scene featuring Jason’s approach begins and the mission truly kicks off. Exit the vehicle and walk toward reception. When you’re close, Jason leans in and asks security for Lucia, starting a cutscene from four months ago.

The cutscene features a call between Jason and Lucia, and Lucia sharing the news about Tomas with Jason for the first time, and ends with Lucia and Jason reuniting at the prison exit.

Return to your car with a very excited Lucia. Depending on what optional missions you accomplished leading up to picking up Lucia, she’ll comment on changes or improvements. For instance, if you’re wearing something rather casual, she’ll note it. Any optional tasks you did complete contribute points toward building your relationship.

Instead of heading home, you’re heading to a party. Drive south back to Key Lento toward the north side of the island, following the GPS to The Rusty Anchor bar. During the drive, Jason asks if Lucia’s aunt can bring down their son for a visit, but Lucia explains that given the situation, it’s currently not possible. They’ve just got to keep their head down and prepare for the future. Lucia suggests that a new friend she made in prison, Kat, might have a lead for them on more lucrative work. Pull into the marked parking spot at The Rust Anchor then head on in to continue.

If you brought Lucia the change of clothes from Andy, she’ll grab the bag and head into the bar with it. Head to the bar while she’s in the bathroom to meet up with Cal who orders three beers. Jason’s crew rolls in and awkward introductions ensue. Lucia goes out back to escape Donnie and Cal and asks for you to grab her another beer. Your next main objective is to speak with the bartender and order her a Pindayho - and another for Jason if you’d like. You can speak with other folks in the bar as you walk back to Lucia.

Delivering the beer kicks off another cutscene where the two spend time catching up. Toward the end, Lucia announces that her rich friend Kat and her husband are on their way, to Jason’s dismay.

The cutscene ends with Jason in the bathroom. I highly recommend using the sink to wash Jason’s hands afterward, not only because it’s sanitary, but also because using the sink gives Jason a Focus buff . Keep an eye out for quick ways to buff stats like this throughout Leonida. It can help in a pinch.

Back at the bar, Cal and Lucia order more drinks and chat. Not long after, Lori and Brian arrive. From here, you can steal Lucia away from Lori (for a small relationship boost) or watch and listen to the other conversations. Lucia gets a call either way and steps out.

This next part is far more casual and there are plenty of folks you can talk to throughout the bar. You’re only required to speak with Cal and Donnie to progress, but if you’d like, walk around and speak with other patrons to learn more about them and get some unique interactions.

Speak with Cal – When you talk with Cal, you can choose to help him swipe through matches on his dating app.

Speak with Donnie – On the other side of the bar, Donnie asks if you want to go out for some coke. You can choose either way. If you choose to, you’ll miss some optional interactions around the bar and it’ll have a negative effect on Jason’s relationship with Lucia.

You can check in on Lucia early to listen in on her call, or you can wait until you get the objective to meet up with her after speaking with Cal and Donnie. She’ll text you. This leads to the “Aviators” walking up and bothering Lucia. You can interrupt (points toward building the relations) or let her handle it (no change). Whatever you do, you don’t have long to decide. Just after, Lucia’s friends Kat and Mattia show up at the bar with not much good to say about The Rusty Anchor. Mattia immediately shows off by spending money, kicking off the party to new heights. Lucia invites Jason to dance, prompting another chance to build the relationship. If you choose to, dance with Lucia by holding L2 + R2 / LT + RT . When prompted, add “flair” to your moves by pressing Square / X .

Not long into the song, Kat and Mattia talk next to Jason and Lucia, before Kat steps back as her baby moves, giving you more interaction options. Another cutscene kicks off with Andy’s arrival. Andy and Lucia’s joyful reunion varies based on whether you met up with her before picking up Lucia. If you want, you can try to improve Jason’s relationship with Andy by speaking to hear at the bar after Lucia walks off to find Kat, or you can try to find Mattia like Lucia asked.

You’ll find Mattia out back on the phone and he won’t want to talk, so it’s best to find him later.

You’ve got another chance to walk around the bar, engage in activities like drinking or dancing, and of course, talk with Jason’s friends. A few are specifically pointed out as objectives:

Donnie – Once again, he’s down for more cocaine. If you accept, time passes again, but again, this will negatively affect Jason’s relationship with Lucia.

Rhonda – Speaking to Rhonda offers an opportunity to dance with her, then help with an important task that’ll improve Jason’s professionalism rating if completed.

Brian – You won’t get an explicit chat option with the very drunk Brian, but you can stand next to him and hear him mumble about kids. You can also listen to him chat with Mattia once he sits down in the next seat.

Andy – She has a short anecdote to share about Lucia when she was young.

To progress, talk to Mattia at the bar or accept Donnie’s offer. If you speak with Mattia like Lucia asked, you’ll start a short cutscene between the two men. Jason starts asking about work, but Mattia shrugs him off. The scene ends with Mattia asking Jason to play pool.

You’ll find pool tables in bars and clubs all around Leonida. This first encounter serves as a brief introduction to playing. Grab a pool cue from the wall next to the pool table with L1 / LB , then approach the end of the table with the white ball to begin.

You can add an optional spin to your shot by pressing and holding Triangle / Y while making your shot.

Use the right thumbstick ( Right Stick ) to adjust your angle.

When you’re ready to shoot, use the left thumbstick ( Left Stick ) or R2 / RT to pull back the pool cue. The amount you move or press the thumbstick or R2 / RT impacts the force of your shot.

Push forward on Left Stick or release R2 / RT to make your shot.

The first pocketed ball determines whether you play as stripes or solids. The assigned type is the kind you want to pocket. When it’s your turn again, you’re placed in front of the white ball you’ll use to shoot. If you’d like, you can move left and right to adjust the starting angle, then repeat the shooting steps to make your move. A preview of the outcome of the expected move shows with transparent white path lines that extend a few inches from the ball, allowing you to estimate what your move will do and adjust as needed. After you take your second turn, the Aviators who were previously hogging the pool table return and hassle Lucia and Kat about their boys taking the table. Continue playing as the Aviators watch and annoy the group. After a bit of time, one of the guys, D-Man, picks up the white ball and interrupts the game. The cutscene kicks off. Mattia and Kat leave while Jason goes out front with D-Man for a fight.

This is a very quick brawl. After knocking out D-Man, two other men step forward to fight. Give them each a few punches, and as you do, Lucia joins in and chokes out the Aviator standing next to her before he can join the fray.

When all men are down, police cars come rolling in, prompting Lucia to excitedly run off, inviting Jason to follow. Run her way and follow her through the neighborhoods. Jason suggests running to the water, ending the escape with a sweet cutscene between the two before they return home.

Back at the house, Lucia walks through as Jason explains it’s still a work-in-progress. She’ll react to the work you did, potentially earning you some extra relationship points between the two. The mission ends the next morning with Lucia leaving for her work detail and Jason receiving a call from Donnie that leads to the next mission, Clean up After Donnie .

With Coming Home complete, you’ll receive the following general mission:

Earn Money – Bring in some money by any means necessary while Lucia deals with her community service.

If you need help thinking of other creative ways to make money, visit our Best Ways to Make Money Early guide . You’ll also have the mission from Donnie to find his package. Completing it progresses the main story .

Have fun with whatever you choose, and if you need additional help making your way around Key Lento and the southern part of Leonida, see these other guides next:

Up Next: Clean Up After Donnie Walkthrough

articles.title: Beginner's Guide - How to Play Dandy's World - Dandy's World [Roblox] Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Dandy’s World is a survival horror game where you will be navigating a dangerous level, attempting to complete machines. While attempting to work on
articles.body:
Dandy’s World is a survival horror game where you will be navigating a dangerous level, attempting to complete machines. While attempting to work on these machines, there are dangerous creatures known as the Twisted who wander around, and if they see you, they hunt you down and chase you. Your goal is to complete the required machines, avoid being caught, and escape the level to proceed to the next one. This beginner’s guide is all about teaching you how to play and survive in Dandy’s World.

The goal of every match in Dandy's World is to complete the required number of machines that you have on that floor. All players start at an elevator and then have to exit to begin searching for these machines. The number you need to complete appears at the top of your screen, and you can see how many machines you have left as they are completed throughout a match. If you’re playing by yourself, you have to navigate the entire stage to find them. If you’re with a group, you’re all working together to complete these machines.

The Twisted wander around the map and only go after you if you’re in their line of sight. When they are, and you’re working on a machine, you’ll be pushed off the machine immediately and have to run away. The Twisted are usually faster than you and force you to use your Stamina, a limited resource. You can use the environment, walls, and other objects to break line of sight with the Twisted and escape.

If the Twisted do catch up to you, they’ll attack you, taking a heart away. All characters have three hearts, and if you lose all three hearts, you’ll be eliminated from the match.

You’ll be able to pick up and use items that are scattered throughout the map to help you. However, you can only hold three items at a time, forcing you to pick and choose the best options for you and your team. These items include helpful consumables, Research Tubes about the Twisted, and Tapes, which are a resource you can use to purchase consumables.

Once all machines have been completed, the elevator opens back up and everyone who is still left needs to race back to it. The elevator will only be open for the timer, and once it reaches zero, the elevator closes. Any player still left on the floor is also eliminated.

In-between matches, Dandy appears with a shop where you can spend tapes to receive items. When the shop does not appear, a list of three available passives shows up that the entire lobby votes on. The passive with the most votes is chosen, and it becomes available for everyone for the rest of the game until it’s over.

The game ends when all players are eliminated by the Twisted or leave the lobby.

When you approach a machine in Dandy’s World, your character will begin to rotate the valve and draw ichor into it. The machine is finished when the ichor reaches the top, and changes from a red light to a green one.

Every so often, you’ll receive a skill check. The type of skill check depends on the machine. The standard ones include stopping a line at a certain point on a progress bar. You want to aim for the grey section, but if you hit the middle, you’ll complete more progress on a machine. Other skill checks include mini-games, such as the Barnaby Machine, which is a Flappy Bird-like game, a treadmill where you can increase progress by sprinting, or a Duo Machine where two players can work together to complete it.

Should you fail the skill check at a machine, it lets out a loud noise, alerting nearby Twisted that someone is working on it. Although your character automatically stops working on a machine if a Twisted gets line of sight on you, if you’re in the middle of a skill check, they don’t let go. You’ll have to choose to finish it or let go and run away.

You can choose what character, also called Toons, you want to play before you start a match. You’ll be able to pick from your available roster, with some characters being better at distracting the Twisted creatures, and some are better at working on the machines.

You can unlock more Toons by visiting Dandy's Shop in the main lobby while you are not in a match. Go to the Buy Toon Licenses page to see all of the available characters. Although you might have enough ichor to purchase one, there are other requirements that you have to meet. For example, Looey is only available if you have 1,000 ichor and you have completed all six of Poppy’s mastery quests.

Every Toon in Dandy's World has five different stats ranked from one-star to five-star, with one-star being the lowest and a five-star ranking being the highest. The five varying stats are: Skill Check, Movement Speed, Stamina, Stealth, and Extraction Speed.

Here's a breakdown of what each stat means, and how they work in Dandy's World.

Skill Check : A higher Skill Check means that the skill check window is larger for this character, how fast the skill check is when the action happens, and how much progress you receive at a machine when you hit a perfect.

Movement Speed : A higher Skill Check determines a character's maximum walking and sprint speed while they are moving around.

Stamina : A higher Stamina means that a character has more maximum base stamina when they start a match

Stealth : A higher Stealth stat means that the Twisted have to be closer to this character to see them and begin a chase.

Extraction Speed : A higher Extraction Speed shows how much ichor a Toon can draw when they are passively working on a machine, outside of skill checks.

Playing as a different Toon not only means that your character's appearance is different, but their stats and playstyle are unique as well. Each Toon has distinct stats and abilities, making them good and bad at specific things during a match.

Boxten, for example, is the starting character and has an average set of stats. Because Boxten is the first character, they do not specialize in anything in particular. Their stats place them in the middle for everything: Skill Checks, Movement Speed, Stamina, Stealth, and Extraction Speed. Boxten's first ability, Wind-Up, is a passive that increases their Extraction Speed by 6% for every alive Toon in the round, to a maximum of 48%. Boxten is a great character to use if you're in a full lobby.

Toodles is slightly different. They're similar to Boxten in that they have average Skill Check, Movement Speed, and Stamina, but have slightly higher Stealth ability and lower Extraction Speed. Although Toodles might not be able to fill a machine as quickly as Boxten, it's much harder for the Twisted to see Toodles, and they need to be closer to start chasing after them. Additionally, Toodles has a different ability called Beginner's Luck, and it's one that requires a player to activate it. When they do, Toodles can roll for a 15% chance to boost a random stat for 10 seconds, and Toodles can do this every 25 seconds.

You'll want to read and learn about a Toon before using them, and also check Dandy's Shop in the main lobby to see what requirements you have left to unlock them.

You can choose to play Dandy’s World in a solo match or with other players when you’re in the main lobby. This occurs in the elevator as a match is prepared for you. When you step into an elevator, you’ll have the choice to continue going, or you can join matchmaking. By choosing to join matchmaking, you’ll be grouped with other players who are also jumping into Dandy’s World.

There are benefits for those who play solo or with other players. When you’re in a solo game, there are fewer machines that you have to complete to progress between the floors. You are also guaranteed to get all of the machines on that floor, as you’ll be the only person who can complete them. However, as you are by yourself, you have to learn how to avoid the Twisted, as you are their only target.

When you’re playing with others, the machine requirement is slightly higher, but not by too much. Since you have multiple players, there’s a good chance people are picking Toons based on a role they’d like to play, such as distracting the Twisted so others can complete machines, and others are focused entirely on finishing them. The downside is you’re not guaranteed to finish a machine, which means you might not get as many rewards at the end of a match, but you can likely progress much further through floors, and at a quicker rate.

The Labs are a separate game mode from the standard matches you play in Dandy World. You can unlock and gain access to the Babs after completing the Dandy's Buds tutorial quests that you receive when first appearing in the game. You'll watch a short video, and then head down to the underground area. Everything is run by Dessa, who is conducting research by observing how you and other players complete floors.

Much of this area and section is the same as a standard match in Dandy World. You'll go down an elevator, explore a floor to find machines, complete them, and avoid Twisteds, while picking up items and Research Capsules along the way. However, rather than having access to Dandy's Shop or passives, you'll receive unique Lab cards from Dessa. These cards are unique passives that apply to all players. Additionally, Dessa may ask everyone to complete experiments on her behalf. These experiments

While you are still earning Ichor for completing machines, everyone also receives Ambrosia for completing each floor. Ambrosia can be taken back to the main lobby and exchanged at Dioda's shop for Ambrosia Vials or Lab-exclusive cards that can potentially be pulled by players. Ambrosia Vials allow you to return to a match if you lose all of your hearts. These can only be used on a Labs match.

Check out these pages for more Dandy's World guides:

Up Next: Progression Guide - How to Unlock Toons Fast

Of course, Disney Dreamlight Valley's Keepsake Sea expansion is filled to the brim with pirates, and perhaps none is more notorious than Captain Hook ! Peter Pan's nemesis is encountered in the Candy Cove biome, where he is up to his old tricks.

Captain Hook is encountered stranded on Donut Island in Candy Cove, as it seems he's lost his ship! You're not sure that Captain Hook can be trusted, but you decide to accept his help searching for Keepsakes regardless!

Captain Hook will move in and join as a Villager after the Quest No Pirates Allowed, settling in Candy Cove permanently.

articles.title: No Pirates Allowed Walkthrough - Disney Dreamlight Valley Guide - IGN
articles.summary: In the Disney Dreamlight Valley Keepsake Sea expansion Quest I Can Speak Whale, you claimed the last Keepsake needed for the Trial of Expression and awakened
articles.body:
In the Disney Dreamlight Valley Keepsake Sea expansion Quest I Can Speak Whale , you claimed the last Keepsake needed for the Trial of Expression and awakened the Guardian. However, things aren't all good - Captain Hook betrayed you and sailed away as soon as you repaired his ship! Now, in the Quest No Pirates Allowed, you must tackle the Trial of Expression and figure out what Hook is up to at last.

Like the previous Trials, the Trial of Expression consists of a series of riddles you must solve by completing tasks similar to Star Path Duties or Dreamlight Duties . There are 15 riddles in total, but you must solve 8 of them to impress the Guardian and earn passage to the Kingdom of Oublié.

The Trial of Expression's riddles are as follows. You can check your progress at any time in the Dreamlight Duties menu.

Once you have completed at least eight riddles, return to the Grotto of Expression. It can be reached by sailing from the dock at Sweetwater Wharf and turning right, then crossing a short stretch of water.

Talk to the Guardian of Expression, who congratulates you on passing the trial. The Candy Cove lighthouse activates, and the passage to the Kingdom of Oublié is open!

Board your ship and sail to the Kingdom. You can do this by going left from the Grotto of Expression. The line of Cursed Anemones blocking your way has disappeared, and you can now sail through the passageway!

Dock at the Coral Coast, which will be on your right shortly after the water turns from purple back to blue. Walk up the stairs opposite the dock to find a large gate.

Unfortunately, the gate is locked - investigate it to read a note saying that a secret passcode is required to open it. A hint suggests looking for hidden symbols around Coral Coast.

Just beside the gate is a large wall with four rotating panels , labeled I-IV. Read the note in front of the wall. It says to count the branches next to the gems on the floor.

Along the railing are four circular decorations, each with a different colored gem in it. Around each gem are a number of white, curling branches. Count the number of branches surrounding each gem.

Using that knowledge, match the rotating dials on the wall to the right gem colors. The solution is:

Go through the gate into Grand Garden. Walk straight forward - in the center of the area is Captain Hook trapped in a cage !

Approach the cage and talk to Captain Hook. Captain Jack Sparrow appears, and reveals that he was the one who trapped the pirate. However, Captain Hook being trapped has caused gates and doors around the Kingdom to close, and you will not be able to progress further without freeing him.

On the left side of Grand Garden, between the gate you came through and the waterfall , is a stone tablet. Pick up the tablet and bring it back to Captain Hook.

Just to the right of the Stone Tablet is a green chest. Inside it is a blue clothing pouch containing the Eel Ruffle Mermaid Arms cosmetic!

Once you give the stone tablet to Captain Hook, Milo Thatch appears and translates it. The tablet contains the Adventurer's Code, and states that no fighting is allowed in Grand Garden, but that disputes are allowed to be resolved over a good meal.

Milo gives you three recipes - read them and cook the listed meals. There isn't a Cooking Station in the currently unlocked areas of te Kingdom of Oublié, but you can place one or return to Shipwreck Shores or Candy Cove, both of which have one.

Pomegranate x 2 - picked from trees in the Kingdom of Oublié

Any Fruit x 2 - an easy option is to simply use more Pomegranates, or Lychees from Shipwreck Shores

Any Sweet x 2 - an easy option is Cocoa Beans, picked in the Glade of Trust or Sunlit Plateau

Unicorn Fish x 1 - fished from white ripples or open water in all areas of the Kingdom of Oublié

Mermaid Gourd x 1 - grown from Seeds purchased at Goofy's Stall in Coral Coast

Any Vegetable x 1 - an easy option is more Mermaid Gourds, or any of the Shipwreck Shores or Candy Cove vegetables

Any Spice or Herb x 1 - an easy option is Luminous Hibiscus, picked in Shipwreck Shores

Twilight Taro x 1 - grown from Seeds purchased at Goofy's Stall in Coral Coast

Wheat x 1 - grown from Seeds purchased at Goofy's Stall in the Peaceful Meadow

After preparing all three dishes, give them to Captain Hook, who of course will still be in the cage in the center of Grand Garden. While the two are able to enjoy a meal together, they keep arguing, and it doesn't free the Captain!

Milo reads more of the Adventurer's Code, and realizes that disputes can also be settled "by fishing rod." Hook and Jack decide to have a fishing contest, with you participating for Captain Hook since he is still trapped.

Captain Hook tells you that a particularly large fish can be found near his ship. The vessel in question is docked on the left side of the Coral Coast, to the left of the dock.

Turn into your merfolk form and swim around to the back of the ship, where there is a gold ripple. Swim through the gold ripple to obtain a Rare Mango Wrasse.

Bring the Rare Mango Wrasse to Captain Hook. The fish are weighed - and it turns out it's a tie!

Talk to Captain Hook again. With no other way of settling the argument, Milo Thatch suggests a truce: Hook's ship will be scuttled and he will be forced to live on land, but Jack will not bother him anymore. The two pirates agree to the truce.

Using Furniture Mode, place Captain Hook's House - actually his ship, the Jolly Roger - anywhere in the Keepsake Sea. Then, interact with the Scrooge McDuck sign and spend 10,000 Star Coins to build the House.

Captain Hook is now unlocked as a Villager - as always, take a photo with him to commemorate it. Talk to Captain Hook to conclude the Quest. He gives you some ominous words: the friend you are here to meet will feel betrayed when they find out you grew up.

articles.title: Palmer Fishing Warehouse Walkthrough - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Palmer Fishing Warehouse is one of two Illegal Operations run by the La Pollila Negra gang in Grand Theft Auto VI. It contains three Key Valuables, including a
articles.body:
Palmer Fishing Warehouse is one of two Illegal Operations run by the La Pollila Negra gang in Grand Theft Auto VI . It contains three Key Valuables, including a luxury watch and a unique weapon variant. This official IGN GTA 6 guide teaches you every Key Valuable location and points out optional items you can grab along the way to maximize your take value.

Click on a link below to jump to that section of this guide:

La Pollila Negra Palmer Fishing Warehouse Location

The Palmer Fishing Warehouse Illegal Operation is located in the southeast section of Bobcat Key, southwest of Grassrivers in Mariana County .

It doesn’t matter how or where you enter; use the main entrance to the north or don’t – it’s up to you.

Immediately after you’re spotted in the compound, you’ll hear some La Pollila Negra thugs shout that they need to get something out of there. Look at the road between the two big buildings and you’ll see a white “SABER SHIPPING” truck start to drive off. Stop the truck, whether by taking out the driver, shooting the tires, or something else, then open the back to find cocaine bricks that you can sell to a fence .

If you're stealthy, you can also get into the back of the truck without alerting anyone. It's parked outside the big building to the east.

There are three Key Valuables in the Palmer Fishing Warehouse Illegal Operation. Click on one below to learn how to get it:

The first Key Valuable – the La Pollila Negra KZ-59 Assault Rifle unique weapon variant – is located inside the big, rusted building in the center of the compound.

Head inside and you’ll see some stairs leading up. Take them up and you’ll be in a fancy upstairs office room. The weapon case is on a table on the north side of the room.

The second Key Valuable is the Crowex Octaine ‘Elite’ luxury watch and it is located in the same room as the La Pollila Negra KZ-59 Assault Rifle .

Look on the small table in the middle of the room to find it.

The third and final Key Valuable is a safe, and it is in the same room as the other two Key Valuables .

Look in the southern corner of the room to find the safe. You either need a safe code or Sticky Bombs to open it.

Palmer Fishing Warehouse Safe Code Location

If you want to use the safe code to open the safe, you’ll need to find it. Starting in the room with the safe, head down the stairs into the room below.

Directly underneath the stairs, there’s a desk with a PC on it. Use L2 / LT to look at the screen; there’s an email displayed that contains the safe code: Tap to Reveal .

Once open, loot the safe’s contents: cash on the top shelf and on the middle shelf.

With all three Key Valuables found, the Palmer Fishing Warehouse Illegal Operation is complete.

Before you leave, go inside the other large building to the east to find six cocaine bricks on a table.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Teaser Shows Magneto Trying to Rip Doom's Mask Off, Leaves Us With More Questions Than Answers
articles.summary: Avengers: Doomsday has a new TV spot, shown in the U.S. overnight, that reveals key new scenes involving Magneto, Doom, Steve Rogers, and Thor.
articles.body:
Avengers: Doomsday has a new TV spot, shown in the U.S. overnight, that reveals key new scenes involving Magneto, Doom, Steve Rogers, and Thor.

The highlight of the TV spot, below, is Magneto desperately trying to use his mutant power to rip Doom’s mask off. "He is pain,” Magneto says. “He is extinction.” “I am Doom," Doom adds.

Unfortunately for our heroes, Doom is so powerful that he’s able to force it back on before his — presumably Robert Downey Jr.’s — face is revealed.

New teaser for ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’. In theaters December 18. — Avengers Updates (@AvengersUpdated) November 26, 2026

New teaser for ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’. In theaters December 18.

But is it actually Robert Downey Jr.’s face underneath the mask? There are all sorts of theories doing the rounds that suggest Marvel may be misdirecting fans about Doom’s true identity in Doomsday. We get a decent look at Doom’s green eyes before he uses his overwhelming power to conceal his face once again. Some are convinced it’s Oppenheimer star Cillian Murphy under the mask. That would be quite the shock given everything we know and have seen about the movie so far.

Earlier this month, Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige confirmed that Doctor Doom is not a variant of Tony Stark in Doomsday . “Is Steve Rogers a Johnny Storm variant?" asked Feige. "People wondered, ‘Is Doom just a variant of another character? Is this just a shortcut to bringing back another character?’ The answer is no. He’s Victor Von Doom.” Is Feige misdirecting fans here?

Why would Magneto try to rip Doom’s mask off in the first place, rather than, say, immediately crush it? Perhaps the plan here is to remove the mask so that Professor X can get in his head? Either way, it doesn’t work.

Avengers: Doomsday Poster Montage Gallery

We also have a new look at Steve Rogers and Thor calmly walking up to Doom in his lair in Latveria. Are they trying to reason with Doom? Do they mean to confront him about his true motivation after some dramatic discovery? Steve Rogers looks pretty mad in this brief glimpse at the scene. Perhaps he feels betrayed?

And finally, we get the shot of Thor trying to hit Doom with Stormbreaker, only for Doom to block the hit with his finger.

Certainly, the more Marvel shows this movie, the more powerful Doom looks. Thanos was a powerful antagonist for sure, but he wasn’t this powerful. I expect the Avengers, X-Men, and The Fantastic Four are in for a rough ride.

Time for some speculation! Lots of people are suggesting there’s something off about Steve Rogers in what we’ve seen of him so far in this movie, to the point where they’re wondering if it’s actually Loki casting some illusion over everyone. We know Loki goes to see Steve and Peggy in what we now believe is The Fantastic Four’s universe to offer his help. Is this the help he was talking about?

We also see Doom’s three Latverian Witches in the new TV spot. While their identities remain a secret for now, fans believe they could be Sylvie, Clea, and Wanda. Are the masks they wear part of Doom’s magic mind control?

Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters December 18.

articles.summary: Dotted around Vice City in GTA 6 are puzzling artworks known as 1010 Murals. There are five of these collectibles to find, and they're tricky to piece
articles.body:
Dotted around Vice City in GTA 6 are puzzling artworks known as 1010 Murals . There are five of these collectibles to find, and they're tricky to piece together, since you need to find both the mural and the correct location to stand to complete it. Note that you need to trigger this treasure hunt first by going on the SnapMatic app on your phone and browsing until you see a post about the artist, 1010.

There are five 1010 Murals to collect, all of which are located in Vice City:

Location: Stand on top of the mark on the roof of the Parlor Apartments on the corner of Northbrook Dr and Santiago Ave and take a picture down into the top of the colorful rainbow building across the street in Rockridge. You can reach this area via an elevator in the lobby.

Location: Stand on the marker on the corner of the roof of the New Quay Plaza building on SE 1st Ave and take a picture of the colorful rooftop below in Downtown. Reach this area by riding the elevator from the lobby to the rooftop.

Location: Stand next to the sign on top of the radio tower on the roof of the Piker Financial Center on SE 2nd Ave and take a photo of the colorful roof below. You can reach this location by taking the elevator to the rooftop and then climbing the tower.

Location: Stand on the mark on the sidewalk near the small parking lot alongside Barlow St and take a photo of the mural built up the southeast corner of the public parking garage in northwestern Ocean Beach.

Location: Stand on the mark on the sidewalk along NE 2nd Ave and take a photo of the mural on the train station while the painted train arrives at the station in central Crosstown. Note that you need the matching painted train to be stopped at the station to complete the mural, so wait for it to arrive.

1010 Murals Reward - Where to Find the 1010 Cheetah

Once you've completed all five 1010 Murals, you'll be sent a clue to find your prize: a custom '95 Grotti Cheetah sportscar. Go to the locked Southside Storage garage (it won't be marked on your map currently) next to the Slator Towing Inc Illegal Operation east of the airport. Approach the garage door to find a keypad requiring a code.

The garage code is 1010 , based on the artist's name.

Enter the code to open the door, unlocking the Southside Garage which contains the 1010 edition '95 Grotti Cheetah for free.

articles.title: Another Modder Uses AI to Make a Multiplayer Mode for The Last of Us Part 2 — Will Sony Shut This One Down, Too?
articles.summary: Another modder has used AI to make a multiplayer mode for The Last of Us Part 2, insisting there isn't much Sony can do about it "even if they do shut me down."
articles.body:
Another modder has used AI to make a multiplayer mode for The Last of Us Part 2 , insisting there isn't much Sony can do about it "even if they do shut me down."

The Last of Us had a brilliant multiplayer mode, with tense gunfights powered by weapon sway, smart cover, and nail-biting in-round crafting that forced you to dig around in your backpack as bullets whizzed over your bonce.

That’s why so many people were excited when Naughty Dog announced a Factions multiplayer game in the works based on The Last of Us Part 2 . Naughty Dog, however, eventually realized that making a live-service game would change the studio forever, and cancelled the project to focus instead on its upcoming sci-fi game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet .

The Last of Us Part 2 made some brilliant tweaks to the combat, allowing for better mobility and deeper stealth. The feel of the weapons, the crunch of the impacts, the audiovisual spectacle of it all was just something else, but we can only experience it in single-player, officially.

It’s no wonder people want to make Factions happen, even without Sony’s approval. And in September, a promising mod made some big strides towards getting multiplayer working in The Last of Us Part 2. As soon as it started to get traction, however, the mod was sent a cease and desist letter from Sony . “Hey everyone, as you all know, the TLOU 2 Multiplayer mod that has been in development since January was supposed to [be released] this month,” wrote creator 'Speclizer' at the time.

“Unfortunately I recently received a letter on behalf of Sony Interactive Entertainment requesting for the mod not to be released. Extremely sad that this never got to see the light of day but I hope you’ll continue to follow me onto the next project, this time something of my own.”

Now there’s a new mod hoping to avoid the eye of Sauron, and it’s already out. The mod is called Twelve Weeks and was built specifically for The Last of Us Part 2 Remastered on PC, using, its creator has admitted, generative AI. Modder 'Kellie' admitted to using Claude code for most of the game's development, and AI was even used to write the lore dumps you can find in the game. The art was, however, made using Blender .

The Last of Us returns with a new online multiplayer mode called TWELVE WEEKS created for The Last of Us Part 2 Remastered on PC. This free mod is a work in progress allowing players to experience a new version of the beloved Factions multiplayer with tactical survival gameplay — 𝗩𝗢𝗬𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗥𝗦 𝗥𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗡𝗚𝗘 (@VoyagersRevenge) November 24, 2026

The Last of Us returns with a new online multiplayer mode called TWELVE WEEKS created for The Last of Us Part 2 Remastered on PC. This free mod is a work in progress allowing players to experience a new version of the beloved Factions multiplayer with tactical survival gameplay

It features reworked levels — Supply Raid and Interrogation for now — with team-based 4v4 combat, new weapons, and character customization. Players can use gadgets like molotovs and smoke bombs, while fighting against other players as the WLF and Seraphites. The mod even adds brutal execution moves. You can grab Twelve Weeks on Nexus Mods .

However, the mod probably won't last long. The modders have attempted to cover their backs with a repository disclaimer that said: "Twelve Weeks is an unofficial fan project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Naughty Dog. The Last of Us is a trademark of its owners. You need your own legitimately purchased copy of the game (Steam). This repository contains no game files and no assets taken from the game."

Will Sony take action? In a reply to someone on YouTube , Kellie said the previous Factions mod got hit by Sony because it was paywalled. "Mine is released already for free and in open source," they said. "Since people have the source code to the full mod already, there ain't much they can do even if they do shut me down."

While The Last of Us Online was canceled, there are hints that Naughty Dog may be ready to return to the series for The Last of Us 3 . And then there is HBO's The Last of Us TV series , which is currently shooting its third (and likely last) season.
