articles.title: New Model Apple iPad Tablets Are on Sale for Black Friday, Including the iPad Mini Released This Month
articles.summary: Mostly erases the price hikes from earlier in 2026.
articles.body:
Apple raised prices on its iPads earlier in June of 2026, but Black Friday is an opportunity to mostly wipe out these price increases. Starting Thanksgiving day, Amazon has dropped prices across the board on the latest generation iPads, from the diminutive Mini to the laptop replacing iPad Pro. Several of these prices are lower than the deals from earlier this week, so even if you think you're up to date on the Black Friday pricing, check again.

November 2026 release; major upgrade over its predecessor

Normally, most iPad updates are incremental CPU upgrades. Not with this update.The Apple iPad Mini is the newest iPad, released earlier this month on November 6. It's a huge upgrade over its predecessor, featuring an gorgeous 8.5" 2316x1512 (326ppi) OLED display, Apple A20 Pro chip with 12GB of RAM, and 128GB of internal storage. This is also the first ever iPad with IP67 dust and water resistance. It's even thinner and lighter than its predecessor, weighing in at a mere 9 ounces. Other new features include Wi-Fi 7, support for Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, and Apple Pencil, Smart Folio compatibility.

The standard iPad is still the the iPad we'd recommend for most people . The current generation model was released back in March of 2025 and features an 11" 2360x1640 (264ppi) Liquid Retina display, A16 chip, and 128GB of internal storage. The combination of a great display, snappy performance, and nearly all the benefits of iOS for under $400 is hard to beat.

The iPad Air was released earlier this year in May. The biggest upgrade is the Apple M4 chip, which is about 20%-30% faster than the M3 chip found on the previous generation model. The iPad Air also supports Apple Intelligence. Apple bumped the iPad Air's memory by 50%, from 8GB to 12GB of RAM. That's enough to run multiple resource-heavy apps, mult-task, and take advantange of processor-intenstive AI features better than before. In addition to increased memory, the iPad also has a brand new N1 wireless chip. For the first time, the iPad Air supports Wi-Fi 7, which offers wireless faster-than-gigabit networking speeds, and Bluetooth 6.

Apple iPad Pro Starting at $1,049 (was $1,200)

The 2025 iPad Pro is currently best tablet on the market, iOS or otherwise, thanks to its M5 processor which is both more powerful and power efficient than its predecessor. It also offers 50% more RAM, faster storage speed, Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 standards, and faster charging. This current generation model features a gorgeous tandem OLED panel. Tandem OLED is better than traditional OLED in two ways: 1) it's far brighter, and 2) it's less prone to burn-in.

Eric Song is the IGN commerce manager in charge of finding the best gaming and tech deals every day. When Eric isn't hunting for deals for other people at work, he's hunting for deals for himself during his free time.

articles.title: South Park Season 29 Has Been Very Flawed, but 'City Endings' Offers a Mostly Satisfying Finale
articles.summary: South Park caps off a very uneven Season 29 with the messy but still very enjoyable finale episode "City Endings." Read our full review.
articles.body:
Full spoilers ahead for South Park Season 29, Episode 6!

There hasn't been a real, concerted effort to build an overarching narrative in South Park Season 29. Sure, certain plot threads have carried forward, like the arrival of Little Randy and Kenny's latest brush with death, but by and large this season has just drifted from one topic to the next. But that doesn't stop Trey Parker, Matt Stone, and the rest from trying to tie everything together in the finale. It's a pretty messy conclusion - a City Ending, even - but a mostly entertaining one.

As was teased throughout this season, everything culminates with November's big event. Not the US midterms, but the long-awaited arrival of GTA 6. Literally everyone in town is busy playing Rockstar's masterpiece, which makes things kind of awkward when it turns out the majority of South America's power grid is being hijacked by billionaire weenies and their data centers.

I definitely would have preferred a more focused and organic approach to weaving together this season's various storylines, but I do appreciate the effort to tie it all together here at the end. "City Endings" does a pretty good job of lampooning all the AI-related headlines that have swirled as of late, from the Jensen Huang/AMD situation to the recent spate of technical meltdowns. It's especially fitting that we see the characters collectively lose their minds over imagined Chinese cyberattacks rather than look inward and realize the problem is coming from inside the house.

It doesn't hurt that the show swings back around to focus on Mr. Kim and the latest evolution of City Wok, which has now been transformed from a clearing house for crappy e-bikes to a sordid massage parlor. It's pretty amusing to watch Kim frantically run around trying to "please" his growing lineup of customers while his disinterested wife goofs off in the back. I complain a lot about the series regurgitating the same jokes over and over, but here I think there's a nice sense of escalation over the course of the episode. I'll also be curious to see if the ending holds and whether Kim returns from his little sojourn in space.

"City Endings" also makes solid use of Butters and his family, as we see how thoroughly corrupted Butters has become thanks to his proximity to power and wealth. We get a fun little parody of The Twilight Zone episode "It's a Good Life," at least until Butters is exposed. That's a great way of paying off on the whole antivax subplot from earlier in the season. There's even a hilariously sad little bit involving Peter and his hapless attempt to insert himself into the Kenny-shaped hole in the group.

Again, this episode is nothing if not chaotic in its attempts to weave all of Season 29's ongoing threads together. There are certain things I would have liked to see more payoff for, including the Little Randy of it all (is this just the ongoing status quo for that character now?). I also felt the Kenny subplot deserved a little more focus than it receives here. But despite those concerns, "City Endings" works as a largely satisfying conclusion to a very uneven season of South Park. And now we don't have to refer to the show as "South America" any longer.

articles.title: Watching TV in GTA 6 Is More Depressing Than Fun, Except for One Show
articles.summary: GTA 6's TV content is impressive on a technical level, but apart from one standout show, it's not all that fun to actually watch.
articles.body:
It seems there’s almost nothing you can’t do in Grand Theft Auto VI, other than solicit prostitutes . Far more than just being a murder and crime spree simulator, the game allows you to kick back and do everything from play basketball to remodel your house to work out at the gym. And yes, that long list of side activities includes watching television.

GTA 6 includes multiple channels of original programming , featuring everything from breaking Vice City news reports to Adult Swim-style animated sitcoms to cheesy telenovelas. As with so much about the new game, the level of detail Rockstar undertook here is impressive. But despite all that, I found that actually sitting down to watch TV in-game wasn’t quite the entertaining experience I was hoping for. If anything, it was a little depressing.

To recap, there are three live TV channels in GTA 6 - the Fox News-spoofing Weazel News, the Telemundo parody Megamundo, and the travel-focused Visit Leonida. For the purposes of this piece, I’m mostly focusing on the former channel. Megamundo is a fun sendup of traditional Spanish-language soap operas, but not having any real attachment to that genre, it’s a joke that only has so much mileage for me. And Visit Leonida is definitely the most limited of the three channels.

With Weazel News, you have a smorgasbord of faux-TV content, all of which focuses on lampooning the right-wing news sector, reality TV, and general American culture. This stream cycles through various breaking news reports, a mockumentary-style series called “The Tyrone Show,” and several different animated sitcoms. And commercials. Dozens and dozens of satirical commercials for all sorts of in-universe products and services.

Initially, you can’t help but sit back and admire the sheer effort that went into making all this content. The TV channels are a very minor feature in the game, and I’m sure many people won’t even really pay attention to them amid all the other countless side activities. The simple fact that you can spend literal hours just sitting in front of a fake TV and not really see any repeat content is impressive.

But once the initial novelty wears off, watching TV isn’t what I’d describe as one of the more rewarding pastimes in GTA 6. Weazel News actually left me feeling a bit stressed out and unhappy after a while. It was hard to put my finger on it at first, but I think what it comes down to is that the political and social satire hits a little too close to home.

For a Scottish-based studio, Rockstar North is generally pretty adept at satirizing American culture with these games - whether it’s remixing the best elements of classic crime films or lampooning the average American’s love of fast food, beer, and guns. You get a heaping helping of all of that with Weazel TV, particularly in the many faux-commercials where colorful characters hawk various brands of alcohol or campaign for a missile launcher in every home or what have you.

The problem is that this material no longer feels as outlandish as it once might have. The sad truth is that real life in the US moved beyond parody at some point in the last 10-15 years. It’s something that a lot of sources of satire have dealt with lately, from South Park to The Onion. How do you top reality when reality has become so unhinged and unbelievable?

GTA’s TV content is in the same boat. A lot of it doesn’t feel particularly far removed from reality anymore. There really are people unironically spouting the same kind of jingoistic nonsense you see in these fake commercials. Between extreme right-wing news channels and the digital hellscape that is social media, there’s a real cultural brain rot that’s taken hold. Watching Weazel TV is more an uncomfortable reminder of where we are as a society than a truly unbelievable parody.

That’s part of it, anyway. The other issue is that some of the Weazel TV humor feels a bit unnecessarily mean-spirited, particularly anything involving the news broadcasts and Tyrone’s sexually charged misadventures. Rockstar really goes all-in on the “Florida Man” humor, mirroring the sorts of kooky regional headlines and weird characters we’ve all read about online. Through the fictionalized state of Leonida, it paints the real Florida as this unending wasteland of deranged hillbillies and unrepentant criminals. And, yes, Florida has more than its fair share of odd residents, but many perfectly lovely people live there also.

I always look to King of the Hill as the gold standard when it comes to satirizing a specific American subculture. That animated sitcom is a clear parody of small-town Texan life, but it never settles for leaning on stereotypes or punching down on its colorful cast of characters. They’re all surprisingly nuanced and fully realized for what might seem at first like a bunch of goofy, beer-chugging rednecks.

GTA’s main cast of characters may get a similarly nuanced treatment, by and large, but the same can’t really be said for the goofballs who appear on Weazel News. Unlike King of the Hill, this TV content does gleefully punch down, and that means it doesn’t fully sit right.

That all being said, there is one good reason to keep Jason’s butt planted on the couch and stay tuned to Weazel News. The channel’s animated sitcoms generally do a better job than the other shows when it comes to providing an amusing dose of escapism. It’s easy to picture any one of these shows having a run on Adult Swim in between reruns of Rick and Morty, whether it’s the stoner humor-focused Macca & Friends or the aggressively copaganda-minded “children’s program” Barnyard Blue.

But the real success story in this area is definitely Right Wing. Right Wing is basically a superhero cartoon about a dimwitted defender of Truth, Justice, and the American Way, or the stereotypical ultraconservative vision of it, anyway. Each episode pits the hero and his handler (a very George W. Bush-coded President) against a different conservative boogeyman villain like the border wall-busting Immigrantasma or the psychically-empowered Educated Woman. Ultimately, Right Wing usually doesn’t save the day so much as he makes a giant ass of himself and exposes the hypocrisy of the anti-left, anti-feminist, anti-LGBTQ+ agenda. All in a day’s work.

Of all the hours of TV content programmed into GTA 6, the Right Wing cartoons are easily my favorite. They’re both hilarious and insightful. The satire works in a way the more direct gags in the rest of the Weazel News content don’t always land. Again, this legitimately feels like something that could run on Adult Swim and find a sizable following in the process.

Only time will tell what sort of additional content Rockstar will add to GTA 6 in the months and years to come. I’m sure the studio is currently heads-down on getting the next version of GTA Online ready for what’s sure to be a historic launch. But I sincerely hope the developer looks at expanding the currently available TV content. There are lessons to be learned in terms of what works and doesn’t work on Weazel News. The main lesson: focus less on trying to satirize the unsatirizable aspects of American culture and focus more on these wonderful little adult cartoons. Season 2 of Right Wing would be much appreciated.

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

articles.title: GTA 6 Players Have Found a Cheeky Method to Quickly Steal ATMs
articles.summary: Somewhere around the middle of GTA 6 you unlock the ability to rob ATMs. Any ATM marked green can be pulled out of the wall and cracked open.
articles.body:
Warning! Potential spoilers for GTA 6 follow.

Somewhere around the middle of GTA 6 you unlock the ability to rob ATMs. Any ATM marked green can be pulled out of the wall and cracked open (check out IGN's guide to all ATM locations in GTA 6 if you need help finding one).

First, though, you need to be able to deal with marked bills through a fence called Yasmini, otherwise the money inside the ATM is worthless and a dye pack will explode in your face. When I got to snatching ATMs, I thought it was cool, but the juice didn’t seem worth the squeeze.

It’s kinda hard to keep things on the downlow when you’re backing a truck up to an ATM, ripping it out of a wall, and tearing down the street with the thing still attached, hoping it’ll burst open and spill its contents onto the street. And when it finally does break open, you have to shoot the money drawers open to get to the goods inside — all for a payout between $6,000-$10,000.

It wasn’t worth the effort, honestly. But there’s a new trick players have discovered to crack those eggs immediately and move onto the next before the cops even know you’re there. I’ve tried it, and like Todd Howard famously once said: it just works.

Here’s what you do. First, you need a truck or other heavy vehicle with a winch attachment at the back. You reverse up to the ATM like normal, and the winch connects to the machine. Now drive forward until the line is taut.

From there, get out of your vehicle and walk up to the ATM with a C4 charge. Hold down aim, and a prompt to place it on the ATM should show up, allowing you to set it on the front with Circle/B. Or throw it at the front of the machine — whatever works.

Once it’s in place, you want to get back in your car and accelerate hard. When it pulls out of the wall, keep dragging it but immediately press unhook, followed by the same button to detonate your charge. It’s important these two actions happen immediately after each other, because the ATM needs to be moving when the explosion happens or the drawers can stay inside the machine.

Done correctly, you can walk over and scoop up the cash and escape before the cops even arrive at the scene. They’ll still be figuring out what happened while you’re hooking up to the next machine, pulling, and sparking up a Cuban. If you need more C4, there’s a free stash of the stuff in the back of Yasmani’s. You can also top up at any Ammunation.

A Simple Trick for Faster ATM Robberies GTA 6 — LUCKY (@Badboy1B) November 25, 2026

A Simple Trick for Faster ATM Robberies GTA 6

Players have been trying to find ways to make quick money in GTA 6 since launch, but most of them are boring exploits. This, though, I can get onboard with because it’s just playing the game as intended in an efficient way, and it’s great fun to slip in and out without the cops getting a whiff of you.

We’ve got the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide here on IGN, complete with comprehensive walkthroughs up to Chapter 4 , guides for the Optional Missions and Illegal Operations you’ll find in Leonida, and much more. Just getting started in Chapter 1 ? Check out our Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , and make a note of the Best Free Weapons to Find Early . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .

articles.title: Creating Fresh Looks Is More Important in GTA 6 Than Any Game Before
articles.summary: GTA 6 has Rockstar's best-ever customisation, with hundreds of amazing pieces. But it's about more that creating a fresh fit - clothes are key to surviving the cops.
articles.body:
This is an opinion piece from writer Jess Kinghorn. IGN's opinion columns represent the personal viewpoints of the writer, drawing on their own experiences and research to explore the exciting world of video games.

There comes a time in every professional criminal’s life when you’ve got to make a dear friend disappear. I’ll keep the spoilers light on when that happens in Grand Theft Auto 6 , but all you need to know is that our man Jason has been tasked with getting rid of a former contact’s car – plus all of their worldly possessions. Now, had I actually checked the trunk I would have seen a bright red gas can and then set the whole thing ablaze – unfortunately, I didn’t check the trunk. Instead, I drove the departed’s wheels straight into Leonida Bay in full view of witnesses. Now, our lad Jason is a wanted man looking to disappear himself.

Camped out in a bush, the police scanner crackles to life. “Suspect is a white male wearing a baseball cap” – well, the cap's the first thing to go, then, as I leg it back to the Ganado. I could keep running and try to outpace the police’s BOLO, but GTA 6 offers a fair few options for escaping suspicion. Losing yourself in customisation and creating a well-stocked wardrobe has become well worth your while beyond simply looking sharp, and it’s now as much a part of your criminal arsenal as carrying a piece.

I didn’t fully appreciate how GTA 6’s wealth of customisation options and the Wanted system interact until chapter two. I was already looking forward to playing dress up with Lucia, so when my new drug-shifting mum-doing-her-best pal Vicki points out the local vintage store, I can’t help but rub my grubby little gamer mitts together.

But besides introducing more fashion options I’m personally inclined towards, chapter two also introduces new crimes to commit. Stick-ups are hit-it-and-quit-it criminal operations – brandish a gun, take the money, and then run. Lucia got her criminal start boosting cars when she was a young teen, so carjacking is a big, lucrative part of this chapter as well. These opportunistic crimes are a complementary contrast to chapter one’s more organised approach – but better yet, Lucia's working for herself rather than Jason playing passive errand boy.

But, my Lucia has too much business to take care of to waste time hiding in bushes, waiting for the heat to subside. Sure, in a stick-up, I can scout around for security camera footage and destroy it like a true professional, or try to control a crowd to stop someone calling the police. Still though, it's tough to be a solo act when Lucia is striking out on her own – given my twitchy trigger fingers have flubbed entering the safe code three times already, I can't rely on making a clean exit every time.

As Lucia pelts out the back door, I keep an ear out for the police scanner on her phone (I’m not gonna think too hard about how that would actually work in real life, and I'm definitely not gonna Google it). Right on cue dispatch says “Suspect is a slim woman in her twenties” (Dispatch, you flatter me), and advises nearby personnel to be on the lookout for someone matching that description, wearing a bandana, a leather jacket, and cargo pants. Well, that’s all the excuse I need to finally check out the vintage store Vicki recommended earlier.

Stashing the bandana and putting on a more friendly face, I use my very recently ill-gotten gains to buy a whole new look. All the usual frumpy suspects are here – well worn trainers, faded sweatshirts, holy-moly jeans – but there are plenty of bangers too. When I’m done, Lucia strides out of the vintage store a whole new woman in a red dress and a pair of trainers a sneaker head would approve of. But diving into a clothes store and improvising a fresh outfit is just one avenue for misdirection.

After a fair few stick-ups, I’ve amassed quite a collection of second hand clothes. Hats, sunglasses, and – like in Red Dead Redemption 2 – bandanas (plus plenty of other 'masks') can be used to hide your face in a pinch. Checking in with the wardrobe at Lucia’s home base, I’ve lost a lot of time composing great fits and saving them for later. It’s a particularly worthwhile time sink as you can then stow these saved outfits in the trunk of your go-to getaway vehicle (for me, that’s an Imponte Ruiner '82 in bright red).

Suspect is a woman wearing a baseball cap and a yellow shirt? Not anymore, she’s not. That’s the secret of any great improviser – they’re not so much making it up as they go along, as they are phenomenally well prepared for every eventuality. And with the way playing dress up in GTA 6 now interacts with the Wanted system, I can play a whole load of different roles.

Customisation doesn’t begin and end with bits of tat you find at Leonida’s second hand shops either. The Wanted system can also keep tabs on how Lucia and Jason’s hair is styled, so popping into the salon frequently is another great shout. There, you can change the style of your protagonist’s hair, the length, and the colour, too – though I do kind of wish I could sling a wig or two in the trunk of my getaway car just to cover all of my bases (especially considering the platinum blonde number Lucia wears in at least one story mission). Still, when she rocks up with freshly braided hair, Jason says he likes the new look – and that’s really what it’s all about.

While Lucia is at it in the salon, she can also play around with make up. The full face looks are pretty limited to begin with, though these – and all other categories of customisation options – open up the more of Leonida you explore. As for Jason, well, we all know facial hair is like contour for men.

Speaking of Lucia’s other half, clothes shopping can also factor into the duo’s relationship. I take the boy to that local vintage spot, Bargain World, and buy him a whole new fit to better complement his shaved-head-incognito-look. Judging by the little pink heart that pops up, Jason appreciates Lucia’s thoughtfulness – and perhaps even enjoys being spoiled from time to time.

With how frequently you’re expected to be committing crimes in chapter two, you’re encouraged to change the look of both protagonists a lot . That’s just as well because every clothing shop, every mom and pop, every salon has different cosmetic options to play with. Heck, even the gun shop offers camo fits and cringe graphic tees (in particular, the image of a smoking shotgun barrel and the words ‘American aromatherapy’ above it sticks in the mind).

I can’t wait to see all Vice City proper has to offer on the customisation front, which promises well-stocked malls and much more. For now though, I’m stuck in Port Gellhorn and making the most of its distinctly down to earth vibe. Don’t get me wrong, I did find some gems at that vintage shop – case in point, I found a graphic vest emblazoned with a pair of fanged, luscious lips and the words ‘Pussycat’ that I kind of wish was in my real life wardrobe.

Unfortunately, the nicest thing I can say about the jewellery selection is that it’s neat you can layer multiple necklaces on top of one another for different looks. To be fair, you can tell a lot about a community based on what turns up in their secondhand shops, and Port Gellhorn’s ‘vintage’ selection goes some way to communicating the dire financial straits many of the locals are in. As such, a fistful of rings that don’t look all that dissimilar to the junk I’ve seen drop shippers flogging in real life will do for a bit of bling right now. Thankfully though, in GTA 6’s criminal sandbox, the next wardrobe refresh is never far.

Jess Kinghorn is a freelancer writer who has written for PC Gamer, PLAY, and GamesRadar+.

articles.title: Rockstar North Chief Was Praying GTA 6's Big Story Reveal Stayed Under Wraps Ahead of Launch
articles.summary: Rockstar North has explained why it was so important that GTA 6's big early story reveal stayed under wraps before the game came out.
articles.body:
Warning! This article contains spoilers for the prologue of GTA 6 .

GTA 6’s prologue hides a surprise that somehow managed to stay a secret all the way up to players finding out for themselves. And Rockstar North, it turns out, was praying for it not to leak ahead of launch.

During the game’s opening stretch, the story of how Lucia ends up in a Leonida prison is told. This isn’t the surprising part — ever since GTA 6 Trailer 1 we’ve known she’d end up behind bars at some point — but the person she was at a diner moments before her arrest is. Tomás, a few-month-old baby and son of Lucia and Jason, is left behind by his mother in GTA 6’s first truly shocking reveal.

Given the history of leaks associated with GTA 6 , it feels like a minor miracle that Tommy’s existence remained a complete unknown until launch. This was something that Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North, was keenly aware of.

“No, we never were going to [reveal it]," he told VGC in an interview that took place just before GTA 6 came out last week. "I am still holding on. Fingers crossed, how many more days? I’m praying it stays under wraps. Given everything that we’ve gone through, every day I’m just like, ‘Please, please don’t do that, please don’t do that.'”

As we’ve written about at IGN, the existence of Tomás in GTA 6 is the key to its whole design . It’s what powers Jason and Lucia’s tale, and encourages the player to strive to make more and more money as those family savings goals get higher and higher. It connects us to the characters, and creates a shared objective between us and them. We aren’t simply committing crime for crime’s sake, but doing so with the prospect of being reunited with their son at the end of it.

You can see why such a powerful and surprising narrative device would want to have been kept under wraps by Rockstar. It’s the first, and by no means the only, shocking revelation of GTA 6, all the more effective when witnessed firsthand.

“We never were going to [reveal it],” Nelson explained. “It’s meant to shock. We were watching everyone speculate about the nature of their relationship and Jason’s character, and that takes it in a completely different context. You have something to strive for beyond a huge bank account at the end.”

articles.title: Rockstar Games Issues Statement as Union Vote Fails
articles.summary: The Rockstar Games union vote has failed, with 75% voting against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union.
articles.body:
The Rockstar Games union vote has failed, with 75% voting against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union.

The shock result comes following the hugely successful launch of GTA 6 , which has set records as the biggest entertainment launch of all time.

Workers at Rockstar Games voted 25% in favour of and 75% against a recognition agreement with the IWGB. The terms of the recognition deal were agreed following months of negotiations that took place even as the IWGB and Rockstar clashed over the firing of 31 workers for allegedly leaking company secrets in October last year. The IWGB has alleged the workers were unlawfully fired, and have accused Rockstar Games of union busting. The vote overlapped with the closing submissions of the employment tribunal, which ended earlier this month. Judgement is currently pending.

Rockstar North and Take-Two Office Protest Photos Nov 2025

If the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union had won the vote, it would have become the biggest recognised union in the UK games industry.

The ballot saw 93.2% turnout, with 1,544 employees across Rockstar’s UK sites in Edinburgh, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee, and London participating. 1,163 team members voted against IWGB recognition (75.3%), while 381 voted in favour (24.7%).

In a statement issued to IGN, Rockstar Games head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, said the company was “extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of GTA 6.”

“This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong,” Kolbe continued. “As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together.”

The IWGB insisted that Rockstar workers would keep organizing without a formal union recognition deal after the ballot.

The IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union shared the following statement:

“For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society — this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.

“Whilst we haven’t emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us.

“A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy. But it’s one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We’ll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs.

“The power to shape our working lives has always been, and will always be, in our hands.”

Kolbe had indicated Rockstar’s willingness to work with staff on union recognition, recently telling Bloomberg : “We go where the team goes. So if they want a union, they will have a union.”

articles.title: Chainsaws 'Would Have Been Too Much' Even for GTA 6, as Rockstar Explains Why Some Extra Violent Weapons Are Missing
articles.summary: Rockstar has explained why some extra violent weapons like chainsaws and katanas are missing from GTA 6.
articles.body:
You can commit an extreme amount of violence in GTA 6 , with a wide variety of weaponry. Guns, baseball bats, even tanks can be your chosen tool of destruction. But that hasn’t stopped some from wondering where some series favourites have disappeared to.

Among those are the likes of katanas and chainsaws, which were staples during Grand Theft Auto’s “3D universe” games, including Vice City and San Andreas. The chainsaw, in particular, holds a special connection to Vice City given its clear Scarface inspirations, and memorable scene involving the power tool from the 1983 movie.

But despite some being spotted around the latest version of Leonida in GTA 6, neither Jason nor Lucia can wield them as weapons. Why? Well, Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson explained the decision in an interview with VGC .

“As far as the chainsaw — I think it would have been too much for this game at this resolution and these characters,” Nelson says. "It’s not a resource thing. Even at the most psycho, did Jason and Lucia really need that — what’s that going to look like?”

When asked specifically about why chainsaws are lying about the world, but can’t be picked up, Nelson explained that, “you’re always trying to find what is the right sort of line and the right balance; it really just depends — you want to feel like you can interact with as much of the world as possible.”

I have to somewhat agree that it just wouldn’t feel like it fit either Jason or Lucia’s characters to be roaming around looking for limbs to chop off with a mechanised serrated blade. Ultimately, their story is one about committing crime to escape to a better, more “normal” life, not one about two psychopaths with a lust for blood going on a rampage.

That being said, when whatever the online component of GTA 6 launches, I could see objects like this becoming weapons, allowing for people to roleplay as whatever brand of criminal, psychopath, or tree sculptor they wish. There’s a world of possibilities out there.

articles.title: Microsoft-Owned GitHub Stuns Followers as It Celebrates AnyPS5 Repo in Now-Deleted Tweet
articles.summary: In a post that’s since been deleted, Microsoft-owned code and software collaboration site GitHub celebrated the AnyPS5 repo “passing 58k stars” from users on the platform as a result of the launch of GTA 6. GitHub even told followers "Happy GTA VImas!" in a tweet that will almost certainly have infurated Rockstar Games, parent company Take-Two, PlayStation, and Xbox.
articles.body:
In a post that’s since been deleted, Microsoft-owned code and software collaboration site GitHub celebrated the AnyPS5 repo “passing 58k stars” from users on the platform as a result of the launch of GTA 6. GitHub even told followers "Happy GTA VImas!" in a tweet that will almost certainly have infurated Rockstar Games, parent company Take-Two, PlayStation, and Xbox.

“GTA 6 is finally here, sparking one of the biggest weeks in gaming and open source on GitHub,” the post said, before jumping into celebrating the repo. “Does changing where games run cross a legal line?” the tweet asked.

This is insane — MVG (@ModernVintageG) November 26, 2026

There was also an official video attached to the tweet, which highlighted a post from an AnyPS5 coder, via Kotaku . The post in the video said: “We have 3 days until GTA 6 everyone[…]get your agents or deevs[sic] and work.”

While the post could easily be the work of a rogue social media person, the optics aren’t good at all. GTA 6 is only officially available on PS5 and Xbox Series X and S, so both Sony and Microsoft have benefited greatly from the game's record-breaking launch. To see a the Microsoft-owned GitHub post a message to its followers essentially encouraging potential piracy is remarkable.

IGN has asked for comment, but GitHub obviously realized its mistake — it deleted the tweet, after all — but how it even got approved in the first place is a mystery until the company comments.

Take-Two is currently working to take down various homebrew community efforts from GitHub, as the race to release an unofficial GTA 6 PC port heats up. This follows Cyberleek's alleged released of the executable file for the incomplete GTA 6 Xbox build they reportedly leaked the week prior. There’s even a website tracking the various attempts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox Series build to PC.

The big question for Take-Two is, can it do anything meaningful to stop a working, playable build of GTA 6 on PC from getting into people's hands? GitHub takedowns can only go so far, as the homebrew scenes uses AI to speed along development. Take-Two stands to make billions of dollars more from the official PC release of GTA 6, so any unofficial version is a significant business risk. In a recent interview with IGN sister site RPS , former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij said that Rockstar Games may be keen to port GTA 6 to PC as soon as possible , due to the explosion of AI-generated clones and ports.

It's also worth noting that there is extra interest in a PC version of GTA 6 because the console versions target 30fps. The PC version, resumably, will run at 60fps or whatever frame rate your rig is capable of .

Earlier this month, Strauss Zelnick, the boss of Take-Two, responded to the threat of AI-assisted reverse-engineering and decompilation of games in an interview with IGN. He said he was taking the issue seriously, and insisted that fans will prefer to play GTA 6 officially, with all its bells and whistles as Rockstar intended, over an unofficial PC version.

IGN: We've seen hackers using AI to clone games much faster than ever before, even try to jailbreak consoles. And there is some concern about this leading to potentially GTA 6 being made available on PC unofficially or places that you aren't releasing it. I was just wondering how much of a threat this is to your business? And, is there anything meaningful you can do about it?

Strauss Zelnick: I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business. I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended.

IGN: Related, last week Anthropic confirmed they took steps to block Claude from reverse engineering video games. I would assume you would welcome that. And would you like to see other AI companies like OpenAI do the same thing to prevent people from using these powerful AI models to clone your games?

Strauss Zelnick: I think all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's. And if you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected.

During an investor-focused Q&A following the release of Take-Two’s latest financial report, attended by IGN, Zelnick was asked multiple times about the AI reverse-engineering problem. He, again, had strong words in response, suggesting Take-Two was ready to lawyer up.

“This business has been largely immune to piracy concerns forever because of file sizes, complexity of piracy, being connected to servers and the like,” he began. “And undoubtedly, it would be very difficult to replicate the experience of consuming our game as intended because of technical limitations.

“That said, it's going to become more of a challenge, as you said, and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. articles.title: Alienware Makes Some of the Best OLED Gaming Monitors Around and They're All on Sale for Black Friday
articles.summary: Backed by a 3 year warranty that covers OLED burn-in.
articles.body:
Alienware OLED gaming monitors are the best displays that you can get for your PC. I currently own and use high-end monitors from several brands, but my favorite monitor thus far is a 39" Alienware 5K OLED monitor. Alienware sources its OLED panels from Samsung and LG and then adds on a 3 year warranty that covers burn-in. For Black Friday , most of Dell's newest 2026 and 2025 monitors have dropped to new price lows and are, in general, more affordable than equivalent Samsung and LG models.

Black Friday Alienware OLED Gaming Monitor Deals

39" Alienware AW3926QW 5K RGB Stripe Tandem OLED Gaming Monitor

32" Alienware AW3226Q 4K RGB Stripe Tandem OLED Gaming Monitor

32" Alienware AW3225QF 4K 240Hz QD-OLED Gaming Monitor

27" Alienware AW2726DM QHD 240Hz QD-OLED Gaming Monitor

39" Alienware AW3926QW 5K RGB Tandem Stripe OLED Monitor

Earlier this year, Dell announced the "world's first 39" 5K monitor with RGB stripe tandem OLED technology."It launched with a retail price of $1,099.99 but for Black Friday you can get it for $100 less . The Alienware AW3926QW has no lack of features that make it stand out from the crowd, but perhaps its most impressive inclusion is the LG RGB stripe tandem OLED panel. Tandem OLED stacks multiple OLED layers on top of each other instead of a single layer. Tandem OLED is better than other OLED panels because: 1) it's much brighter (the AW3926QW in particular has a very impressive 1,300 nits of peak brightness) and 2) it's less prone to burn-in.

The AW3926QW doubles down on this with new RGB stripe technology. Whereas traditional tandem OLEDs use white pixels, RGB stripe tandem OLED breaks the color down further into vertically aligned red, green, and blue pixels. This reduces color fringing and in turn significantly improves text clarity. It goes without saying that there are obvious benefits here for both gaming and productivity purposes alike.

32" Alienware AW3226Q 4K RGB Tandem Stripe OLED Monitor

The 32" Alienware AW3226Q gaming monitor is another recent release that's aimed toward the more budget-conscious crowd. The monitor launched about a month ago at a very reasonable $699.99 price tag, but it's already $150 off for Black Friday. Unlike the slighty more expensive AW3225QF which uses a curved 240Hz QD-OLED panel from Samsung, the Alienware AW3226Q is equipped with a flat panel 165Hz RGB stripe tandem OLED panel from LG. In exchange for a lower refresh rate and no official G-Sync certification (it's still G-Sync compatible), you get better text clarity and arguably a better monitor for non-gaming use.

Alienware's most popular 4K OLED gaming monitor is also down to its lowest price ever. For Black Friday, you can pick up a 32" Alienware AW3225QF 4K QD OLED gaming monitor for just $699.99 with free shipping. The AW3225QF is a rare gaming monitor that combines a native 4K resolution, 240Hz refresh rate , and a gorgeous Samsung-sourced quantum dot OLED panel. If you're looking for the best 4K gaming monitor , this should definitely be on your short list. The Alienware AW3225QF is HDR True Black 400 certified with up to 1,000 nits of peak brightness. It also boasts a factory calibrated 99.3% DCI-P3 color range, 1700R curve, and G-Sync certification .

27" Alienware AW2726DM QHD QD-OLED Gaming Monitor

Most people would agree that OLED monitors are as good as it gets for gaming. They're also really expensive. Well, Alienware is bucking the trend with one of its latest 2026 OLED releases. The 27" Alienware AW2726DM QHD 240Hz QD-OLED gaming monitor is listed at an already reasonable retail price of $349.99, but for Black Friday it's down to just $279.99 with free shipping. This is a 27" 2560x1440 (QHD) monitor that incorporates a Samsung quantum dot OLED ( QD OLED ) panel, which is brighter and has a wider color gamut than the more commonly found W-OLED panel.

27" Alienware AW2725D QHD QD-OLED Gaming Monitor

At first glance, the AW2725D appears to be very similar to the AW2726DM albeit at a higher price point. There are two primary reasons for this, however. (1) The AW2725D boasts a higher 280Hz refresh rate and (2) it has official G-Sync certification.

articles.body:
Mount Soulrend is the final location in Phantom Blade Zero , and it features the last bunch of Memory Flowers in the game. This is one of the few types of collectibles that you'll find — there are no Blackstone Fragments or Sha-Chi Amber Shards . So, let's dive deep into this guide and look for the last Memory Flowers in Mount Soulrend.

There are 6 Memory Flowers in Mount Soulrend. Check the map above for their general location and the rest of the guide for the individual spots.

As you enter Mount Soulrend, you’ll see the first flower right away , before you enter the temple. It’s on the left side of the path, next to praying statues.

This is Memory Flower of the Monster I - Scrawny Leg .

From the Mountain God Temple checkpoint, exit the building and go to the right side. You’ll find a linear path; go forward until you reach a narrow bridge. The flower will be on the way, with crows around it.

This is Xuan Li’s Memory Flower IV - Meng Hua .

From The Last Mandate Encampment bell, keep moving forward to the west side of the region . You’ll descend to lower ground and be below a cliff with pillars. The flower will be in the middle.

This is Xuan Li’s Memory Flower V - Fused with the Blight .

Shortly after the previous flower, this one will be on the main path, after you jump over a broken bridge using your hook . You’ll see the flower on your left, next to a tree. It’s right before the Frostcliff Cavern .

This is Memory Flower of the Monster II - Infighting .

As you descend into the Frostcliff Cavern, you’ll find The Giant’s Lair checkpoint. Instead of moving forward and climbing a marked wall, turn right, and you’ll see the flower at the end of the frozen lake .

This is Memory Flower of the Monster III - Mastermind .

Once you have defeated The Saw and the Crusher in The Giant’s Lair, keep going on the only path available, and you’ll reach a small stone bridge . The last flower will be there.

This is Xuan Li’s Memory Flower VI - Control .

articles.body:
Manni L. Perez, the actress who plays Lucia in GTA 6 , has issued her first statement since the game came out.

Perez’s role as Lucia Caminos was confirmed when she was nominated in the Best Performance category for this year’s The Game Awards , a day before GTA 6 launched on November 19. She’s now considered the favorite following the game’s critically acclaimed, record-breaking launch.

Now, a week later, Perez took to social media to thank fans for the reception to GTA 6.

“Life has been such a whirlwind these past couple of days and I just want to take a moment to say thank you,” an Instagram Stories post began.

“Thank you to all the new followers, to all the beautiful messages, and the positive reception the game and my character have received.

“I've dedicated almost a decade bringing Lucia to life. She's been such a significant part of mine and I am beyond grateful she now gets to be a small part of yours.”

Perez is an actress with a smattering of credits to her acting resume, including TV guest roles in Jessica Jones, Chicago P.D., and Law & Order: Special Victims Unit. While she hasn't been up to much else over the past few years, it's easy to know why — GTA 6 sounds like it was a pretty involved project. Indeed, Lucia isn’t Perez's first GTA role. In GTA 5, she plays the background character of "Clubber #2," while in GTA Online she voices a blackjack dealer.

Meanwhile, Jason actor Dylan Rourke also posted a message of gratitude on Instagram Stories, saying: “Thankful for this wild ride. Gratitude won’t cut it. Make today about the ones you love.”

Manni L. Perez shouldn't be confused with Manny Perez, who plays Raul Bautista in GTA 6. This week, Manny Perez bought a PS5 just so he could play the game, saying in a video posted to social media: “Guy, I’m playing and this s**t is crazy! Look how real that looks. I’m learning, I’m loving this, it’s crazy.”

Other GTA 6 actors who've started to talk about their work on the game include Lexie Shoaibi, who recently spoke out about her "bittersweet" newfound fame after her character, Mandy, went viral online, and Cocoteo FM radio host Issa Lopez, who described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game .

articles.title: Floating nature islands installed in Glasgow parks as Games legacy
articles.summary: The islands, being planted in five Glasgow parks, are designed to encourage wildlife and help clean the water.
articles.body:
Floating islands are being installed on ponds in five of Glasgow's parks as part of the 2026 Commonwealth Games legacy.

The islands, which are being planted by community groups, are designed to encourage wildlife and help clean the water.

The project will create almost 250 square metres of new wildlife habitat which is expected to last about 20 years.

Glasgow 2026 organisers say they are funding the projects as part of their commitment to greener games.

The islands are manufactured by a Moray-based company which has been exporting them around the world.

Biomatrix Water Solutions in Forres has installed islands in Boston, Venice and London.

They have also been floated onto the River Clyde at the Glasgow Science Centre as part of an unrelated project.

The new islands are being installed at Victoria Park, Elder Park, Richmond Park, Queen's Park and Hogganfield Loch.

Ellen Hebdon, the company's operations manager, said the plants' roots played an important role in preventing and removing harmful algae from the water.

"It's not an overnight solution, but over a period of time, you will see benefits in the clarity and the cleanliness of the water," she said.

The islands are made up of recycled plastic materials, including drinking water pipes, to create buoyancy and are held together using marine-grade stainless steel.

They are then topped with a lightweight clay aggregate, called leca, into which the plants are inserted.

The aquatic plants include a mix of evergreen and flowering native species such as marsh marigolds, water forget-me-nots and ragged robin.

Their roots underneath the islands provide shelter for aquatic wildlife.

The location, in the middle of the water, also provides nesting spaces for birds, which would be largely free from disturbance.

Local schools and "friends of the park" groups are helping with the planting and maintenance.

Games organisers say sustainability is an important delivery factor with all competition venues powered by renewable electricity and electric or hybrid vehicles making up two thirds of the transport fleet.

Glasgow 2026's head of sustainability, Selina Donald, said the city council had been looking at creating floating islands but did not have the funding.

"I really saw the pride in all the parks, the pride in the green spaces, the pride in the natural environment across the city," she said. "And so really, for us, it was a way that we can celebrate and support that."

articles.title: After Playing Infinity Nikki 3.0 for Four Hours, its New Cities and Outfits Are Just Some of the Additions Worth Returning For
articles.summary: The new 3.0 update has tons of new stuff to explore including new locations, outfits and gameplay systems, although don't expect any kind of proper challenge.
articles.body:
When Infinity Nikki first launched in 2024, it introduced players around the world to the dress-up world of mobile game star Nikki in her first 3D console/PC adventure, an open world filled with wholesome fun, fashion and friendship. 2025’s V2.0 update introduced a new area to the world of Miraland, as well as new ways to traverse it. But now with the new V3.0 update titled Of Yesterday and Tomorrow, Nikki’s wonderful world has been expanded significantly – with its richest locations yet, and even a cute convertible to traverse it with.

To give you an idea of how huge this update is, I played for over four hours at developer Infold’s Shanghai office, focusing mainly on story content and with only the slightest bit of open-world exploration and lifestyle simulation gameplay, and didn't even see all of one of its two new cities. The golden path apparently offers some nine hours of story content, with two dense and exciting new areas to get lost in. Between the V3.0 launch and Nikki’s birthday celebration campaign, players can get 160 free draws and 19 new sets of clothing.

I spent most of my time in Cicia, a city of art, based loosely on Paris among other places, and lined with cobblestone streets and beatific brickwork architecture. Cicia was previously featured as a location in the mobile game Shining Nikki, and makes its 3D debut here. It’s a world where art nouveau, belle epoque and art deco collide, and home to the Cicia Art Academy where Miraland’s most promising students are taught lessons of art creation and appraisal by the finest tutors. When Nikki receives an invitation to study there, she and her catlike companion Momo embark on a new adventure of aesthetic discovery. But is everything at the academy truly as it seems?

Some of the outfits in the update grant Nikki new skills. Unlock and craft the preppy four-star Leaping Breeze outfit to gain a higher double-jump and airborne dash abilities, while the much darker and sexier Night’s Hidden Side outfit allows Nikki to “bind” with objects around the environment (think Mario’s possession skill in Mario Odyssey) and use them to warp to hard-to-reach places. These new skills allow for a new level of verticality in Cicia’s map and dungeons, helping you explore the castle spires or negotiate intricate dungeon maps.

You can also find a musket for long-range attacks (which is a new Whimtech item), and dress for the occasion in Cicia’s three-star, nine-piece outfit Song of Endless Youth.

V3.0 also introduces a new outfit category, Star Crown Resonance. The Star Crown Resonance outfit named Where Stars Shine Again comes with a musket and staff, and is designed for tougher combat situations. With either weapon equipped, Nikki’s unused dashes are stored, and you can release them all at once or use them one at a time, creating a sort of combo system that deals more damage.

While previous Infinity Nikki maps tended towards countryside locations, Cicia is a bustling city. Arriving by airship to take in the stunning views, Nikki and Momo step into a throng of students, teachers and residents, each with voiced dialogue to idly eavesdrop on as they prepare for a huge school festival, building an air of excitement as Nikki starts academy life. In this maelstrom of culture, recruiters for the drama club and literature club compete for Nikki’s attention.

And then she meets Béatrice Laviolette. A young ducal heiress, at first Béatrice is quite brusque, standoffish and snobby. It started to feel like meeting Glinda in the heightened magical environs of Shiz University, and when it was announced in a cutscene that the students would compete for the right to wear a legendary Miracle Outfit, I assumed Nikki and Béatrice were heading into a bitter rivalry. But Nikki has always been a relentlessly positive character, with a deep and forgiving heart and a desire to encourage those around her. Without wanting to spoil anything, let’s just say that she, Béatrice and earnest classmate Déphine Garnier foster a relationship that may surprise you.

Meanwhile, fellow student Sikong Ran invites Nikki to join his Society of Whispers and Wonders, a supernatural-obsessed group who study things that go boo in the night – lending more than a little taste of Wednesday or Riverdale high-school mystery.

Exploring the city is a reward unto itself. Rich and bustling with life, it features picturesque sunsets, glittering lakes, colourful flowerbeds, gargling fountains. It is filled with side missions and simple minigames, including one where you construct a street band to perform jolly jazz music in the castle plaza. In the streets, teachers guide students through artistic concepts that are interesting to read – for example, did you know that in music, technical perfection is no match for the heart of the musician? The characters you meet are endearing; and as before, the dialogue is filled with gentle humour – not least the central relationship between Nikki and Momo, which remains as heartwarming as ever.

But as you progress, Nikki learns that behind the magic of this idyllic city, there is a dark secret. Using her new binding skill to unravel environmental puzzles, she is drawn into a conspiracy that only Nikki can solve.

As part of this, I got to play through one of two new dungeons, titled The Ideal City. This is a clockwork house of tricks that recalls the steampunk-coded vibe of earlier Infinity Nikki dungeons, with huge cogs that alter the mechanical environments as they turn, and wooden theatre dioramas folding in and out of view in the background as you progress.

Half of the exploration takes the form of platforming action, which, like previous Infinity Nikki dungeons, is not exactly a tough challenge, but enough to make use of Nikki’s new jump and dash abilities and test your reactions a little. The other half is made up of environmental puzzles that use Nikki’s new bind ability, tasking you with scanning the area of objects to possess and manipulate in order to progress – for example, turning keys or bouncing between bird-shaped statues on high-up ledges. In one section, you even possess a giant glass marble and manoeuvre it along tight, narrow ledges, like Super Monkey Ball. The variety of gameplay on offer is strong, and, combined with the fantastic art design and hummable jazzy soundtrack, makes up for the lack of a tougher challenge.

Speaking of which, I also got to try a boss battle from later in the campaign, making use of Nikki’s battle-ready Where Stars Shine Again outfit for more powerful combos. I was able to beat the boss on my first try. But Infinity Nikki isn’t really supposed to be a hardcore action experience, and the drama of the scene and the story beats that lead up to it should satisfy fans, while offering some mild challenge to younger players.

Also in Cicia, I got to try the new driving system. Up until now, Nikki has largely travelled on foot or by bicycle, but now she has a range of vehicles to choose from – and fun ways to use them. You can get your own convertible, pay in-game currency to rent a classic car, and unlock even more. While driving, you can change the radio stations like in GTA, engage in Uber-style mini-missions like in Crazy Taxi, or simply drive to your destination. The car even has a jump button.

But what impressed me the most is how photo mode has been integrated here. Infinity Nikki has had a strong photo mode since launch, allowing players to dress and pose Nikki and Momo to their satisfaction and snap them at will. I wondered if it would work while she was in the driver’s seat – and I was pleasantly surprised to find that not only does it work, it comes with a wealth of car-specific customisation options – such as opening or closing the doors, switching the head lamps on or off, and raising or lowering the convertible roof. These thoughtful touches enhanced my time spent with Nikki on the road, and show just how much care and attention have gone into this new update.

Did I mention that Cicia is only one of two new areas? I spent just a little bit of time in Ceremius, a city with more of a dark fantasy style. Here a terrible earthquake has upended the city, while some magical force has held it together in surreal ways. But while the post-disaster atmosphere is undoubtedly more sombre and intense than in Cicia, the city is still densely populated with residents. The art theme also remains, with a plethora of statues and installations to find. Clicking on one bizarre statue, I got a paragraph of smartly written critique, explaining the work with the eye of an art collector.

Ceremius also features a new set of alchemy abilities, which I didn't have time to try, but promise to add even more depth to an already packed content update.

During my time with Of Yesterday and Tomorrow, it was a pleasure to return to Nikki’s fashion-friendly world. In particular, Cicia and Ceremius are introduced in impressive detail, and I felt like I was not only exploring a real place, but enjoying the design team’s eye for art as well, as the story presents artworks, fashion and musical theatre in a way that actually lets you experience them directly. The update drops today, so jump in and dress up to see for yourself.
